Strong H$α$ emission (EW$_{\rm rest}\simeq880$ Å, $\logξ_{\rm ion}\simeq25.3$), a blue UV slope ($β_{\rm UV}\simeq-2.5$, down to $\simeq-3.1$ in the core), and a Balmer decrement consistent with no dust attenuation indicate a young ($\lesssim10$ Myr), dust-free burst. [OIII]$λ$5007 is not detected in the integrated spectrum, implying [OIII]/H$β\leq0.61$ ($3σ$) and, using an extrapolated strong-line calibration, $12+\log({\rm O/H})\leq6.4$ ($\lesssim0.5\%\,Z_\odot$). This places LAP2 among the most metal-poor galaxies known. Faint [OIII] emission is, however, detected in the core (with $\rm4σ$ significance), where we derive $12+\log({\rm O/H})\simeq6.6$ ($\sim1\%\,Z_\odot$). This difference can be explained either by local self-enrichment, requiring only $\rm \sim0.2\,M_\odot$ of newly synthesized oxygen, or by a higher ionization parameter in the core. The upper limit on HeII$λ$1640 (EW$_{\rm rest}<39$ Å, $3σ$) does not exclude a contribution from metal-free stars. LAP2 extends the census of spectroscopically confirmed EMPGs to star-cluster masses and to $M_{\rm UV}\approx-13$. Its location in a low-density region supports a scenario in which underdense environments preserve nearly pristine gas well after reionization.

title: Developing the Field Selector System for the SHARP Multi-IFU: Optomechanical Design and First Prototype Validation
comment: 11 pages, 15 figures, published on Applied Optics
summary: This paper presents the innovative Field Selector System (FSS) developed for VESPER, the multi-Integral Field Unit of the SHARP near-infrared spectrograph. The proposed system employs an array of movable light-collection probes (Field Selectors) that travel along parallel, vertically offset planes to avoid mechanical interference and vignetting. The true novelty lies in its opto-mechanical synchronization: as each probe translates by Δy to select a target, a set of folding mirrors shifts by Δy/2. This maintains a constant optical path length, allowing multiple independently moving probes to share a single focal plane and form a continuous image on it, easy to slice by the slicer. A dedicated optical test setup was developed to characterize the positioning stability and repeatability of the probe motion. The measured mechanical errors were converted into equivalent optical tilts and incorporated into the SHARP optical model to assess their impact on instrument performance. The experimental results identified the dominant sources of positioning error and provided valuable insight into the relationship between mechanical tolerances and optical performance. The study also highlights several design improvements capable of significantly reducing probe tilting and enhancing system stability. The results demonstrate the viability of the proposed concept and indicate that, with the identified improvements, the system represents an excellent field-selection solution for SHARP and other multi-integral-field-unit (mIFU) spectrographs.

title: Probing CP Violation in the Complex 2HDMS with a 95 GeV Scalar at Future $e^+e^-$ Colliders
summary: In this study, we investigate the prospects for probing CP violation in the complex singlet extension of the two-Higgs-doublet model (2HDM) at future electron-positron colliders. In extended scalar sectors, cancellations among different contributions to electric dipole moments (EDMs) can relax the stringent constraints on CP-violating phases, potentially bringing them in the current reach of collider experiments. We consider a scenario in which both the 125 GeV Higgs boson and the additional scalar associated with the reported 95 GeV excess are CP-mixed states. We probe the CP-violating phase of the 95 GeV scalar through its production via Higgsstrahlung and subsequent decay into a tau-lepton pair, using a CP-sensitive forward-backward asymmetry in hadronic and semileptonic tau-decay channels. We estimate the sensitivity at future lepton colliders, namely the ILC, FCC-ee, and CEPC, and investigate the impact of the Standard Model Drell-Yan background. We find that the hadronic channel offers greater sensitivity than the semileptonic channel. We also compare our results with existing constraints and future projections for CP violation in the 125 GeV Higgs sector and briefly discuss the implications for electroweak baryogenesis. Our results highlight the potential of future lepton colliders to probe CP violation in extended scalar sectors while remaining consistent with current EDM constraints.

title: Horndeski Gravity as an Effective Dark Energy Fluid in Cosmological N-body Simulations
comment: Master thesis, Universidad de Chile (FCFM, DFI), defended 30 Jun 2026. 108 pages, 13 figures
summary:
Unraveling the nature of the cosmic expansion, driven by Dark Energy (DE), remains one of the key challenges in modern cosmology. Modified Gravity (MG) models provide an alternative to the standard cosmological constant paradigm. These models predict distinct signatures in the growth of structure, yet analytical predictions are challenging due to the highly non--linear equations involved.
  To overcome this problem, we study MG as an effective DE fluid. To this end, we have incorporated linear DE perturbations into the N--body code $\texttt{CO}N\texttt{CEPT}$, which relies on the Einstein--Boltzmann solver $\texttt{CLASS}$. We replaced the $\texttt{CLASS}$ version used by $\texttt{CO}N\texttt{CEPT}$ with $\texttt{mochi\_CLASS}$, a patched version that includes Horndeski family models. By writing linear DE perturbations ($δρ_{\rm DE}$, $δP_{\rm DE}$, $θ_{\rm DE}$, and $σ_{\rm DE}$) in terms of metric perturbations in the synchronous gauge, the N--body code is able to evolve the effective fluid using the Boltzmann equation. Our current simulations encompass a range of cosmological scenarios ---$w_0w_a$CDM, Hu--Sawicki $f(R)$ and cubic Galileon--- each extended to include massive neutrinos.
  For each of the models, we have found deviations from General Relativity close to what is predicted in the linear regime: a sub-$0.2\%$ relative difference for $Λ$CDM, up to $40\%$ for $f(R)$ and a sub-$25\%$ for cubic Galileon. Since our code is the first to implement Horndeski gravity into an N--body code, its validation is a non--trivial computational task. Our novel code opens the door to explore a vast number of modified gravity models in the context of current and future cosmological surveys.

title: Gluon and Faddeev--Popov ghost propagators in rotating background: An eigenfunction approach
summary: We construct the free gluon and Faddeev--Popov ghost propagators in rigidly rotating cylindrical coordinates using an eigenfunction approach within the Feynman gauge. Starting from the quadratic gauge-fixed QCD action, we derive the corresponding kinetic operators and obtain their spectral representations. For the gluon field, a circular polarization basis diagonalizes the vector wave operator, leading to polarization-dependent shifts in the orders of the radial Bessel functions. In the absence of radial boundaries, we explicitly recover the standard Minkowski propagator in inertial Cartesian coordinates, showing that the off-diagonal tensor components in the cylindrical basis have a geometrical origin. We then extend the construction to a finite-radius cylinder satisfying the causality condition $|Ω|R<1$, imposing relative boundary conditions on the gluon field and Dirichlet conditions on the ghosts. The resulting discrete transverse spectra involve both Dirichlet and Neumann eigenvalues for the gluon modes, from which we obtain explicit spectral representations of the propagators. Our results provide a consistent framework for perturbative QCD calculations in rotating geometries, retaining the angular-momentum, polarization, and boundary effects relevant to future studies of correlation functions and radiative corrections.

title: Topology change and the Gauss Bonnet term in causal set theory: the sign of the cosmological term and the axion decay constant
summary: Causal set theory permits changes of spatial topology without the metric degeneracy that forbids them in continuum Lorentzian gravity. In four dimensions such changes enter the gravitational action only through the Gauss--Bonnet term, which is the Euler density. We show that the Euler density of a discrete space is exact, local and combinatorial: it sums to the Euler characteristic at any resolution and is supported on topological defects. The Gauss--Bonnet term of a causal set is therefore fixed rather than postulated. Because it is linear in the number of elements, which is the four-volume, it acts as a cosmological constant. Its coefficient follows without forming any functional derivative, so the known obstruction in the continuum does not arise. The everpresent cosmological constant of causal set theory assumes that the mean topological charge vanishes. We show that it does not. The species of opposite sign solves the field equations only if a positive cosmological constant is already present, and, being simply connected, it cannot carry the axion charge that supports the other species. Only one sign survives, and the sign of the cosmological term is derived rather than assumed. We recover the surviving transition from the causal order alone in every simulated sprinkling. The action of the corresponding axion wormhole then fixes the magnitude. The observed value requires an axion decay constant near the grand unification scale, and this result is insensitive to the one-loop prefactor and to the Gauss--Bonnet coupling.

title: She Sees Shells by the Stellar Shore: A Kinematic View of NGC 253's Stellar Halo
summary: The stellar halos of nearby galaxies are fossil records of ancient mergers, providing insight into the formation and growth of these systems. These halos often contain substructure in the form of streams, shells, and debris fields that make up dynamically young remnants of past accretions. These remnants can be probed with resolved-star spectroscopic observations, giving insight into the kinematics of bygone satellite companions. Such observations have been made for the Milky Way (MW) and Andromeda, but are much more challenging and expensive to do outside the Local Group. The Local Volume has an abundance of MW-mass galaxies with richly structured halos, such as NGC 253. Leveraging the power of Magellan's M2FS fiber-fed multiobject spectrograph, we have obtained medium-resolution spectra of 225 stars centered on NGC 253's southwestern shell. These spectra enabled us to make the first-ever measurement of the resolved-star stellar kinematics for 89 stars in NGC 253's halo. We also detect substructure in several ways and identify regions likely to be accreted and in-situ, finding among them a low-velocity region coincident with the previously reported SW shell we believe was accreted recently, and an in-situ component that traces the outer disk. After subtracting NGC 253's systemic velocity, we measure median line-of-sight velocities of $-34_{-12}^{+16}$ km/s and $167_{-14}^{+16}$ km/s for the accreted and in-situ populations, respectively. This work highlights the utility of kinematics to differentiate between accreted and in-situ stars, and acts as a pathfinder for future observations with next-generation 30 m telescopes and wide-field multiobject spectrographs.

title: SHARP: A spectrograph proposal to fully exploit ELT capabilities
comment: 12 pages, 6 figures, proceeding of SPIE 2026 - Ground-based and Airborne Instrumentation for Astronomy
summary: The Extremely Large Telescopes (ELTs), with their large apertures and cutting-edge Multi-Conjugate Adaptive Optics (MCAO) systems, promise to deliver data sharper and deeper than even the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) across large fields. SHARP is a concept study for a near-IR (0.95--2.45 $μ$m) spectrograph specifically designed to fully exploit the collecting area and angular resolution capabilities of the upcoming ESO's ELT. The instrument concept is driven by the goal of tackling the most important questions in astrophysics and cosmology, bridging the gap between the local and distant Universe. This requires versatility to accommodate diverse observational needs. SHARP (http://sharp.brera.inaf.it) is composed of two main units: NEXUS, a Multi-Object Spectrograph (MOS) optimized for detecting the faintest sources, and VESPER, a multi-object Integral Field Unit (multi-IFU) designed for brighter ones. This presentation provides an overview of the scientific design drivers, the solutions developed to meet them, and the resulting optical design that achieves the required performance.

title: The Cosmology of Hawking Axions
summary: Since primordial black holes (PBH) are always non-relativistic, their cosmological energy fraction grows relative to that of radiation. Thus, for even a tiny initial PBH abundance, the universe generically enters an epoch of early matter domination, which ends when the PBH evaporate to restore the hot big bang. We consider the possibility that a PBH dominated era yields a population of boosted axion-like particles (ALPs) produced from Hawking evaporation. Eventually these ``Hawking axions" become non-relativistic and decay to photons, which can affect various cosmological and astrophysical observables. Here we place new constraints on these particles through their impact on big bang nucleosynthesis, cosmic microwave background, large-scale structure, and X-ray observables. Furthermore, if Hawking axions remain relativistic through recombination, then depending on the progenitor PBH mass, they contribute $ΔN_{\rm eff}\simeq0.05$-$0.11$, which may be observable with future CMB probes.

title: Planting neutrino SE-EdS: A < 3% accurate clustering approximation for neutrinos and other hot dark matter
comment: 37 pages, 16 figures. Code available at https://codeberg.org/upadhye/SE-EdS
summary: The age of the cosmic neutrino is upon us. Aside from their fundamental importance to particle physics and the recent tensions in their mass scale $M_ν= \sum m_ν$, neutrinos' degeneracies with other cosmological parameters in analyses of scale-dependent cosmic clustering will significantly affect the estimates of these parameters, making accurate, inexpensive, easily-implemented approximations essential tools for theoretical cosmology. We present a new linear approximation, SE-EdS, applicable to non-relativistic neutrinos and other hot dark matter, which is exact in the linear Einstein-de Sitter case, and < 3% accurate for a broad range of flat and non-flat cosmologies characterized by parameters $0.2 \leq Ω_{m,0} \leq 1$, $0 \leq Ω_{ν,0} \leq 0.018$, $-0.1 \leq Ω_{K,0} \leq 0.1$, and $w_0 \leq -0.6$, at all length scales. This broad coverage in $Ω_{m,0}$ makes SE-EdS ideal for N-body simulations, whose redshift range $z \lesssim 100$ demands accuracy for time-dependent $Ω_m$ between unity and the preferred late-time values $\sim 0.3$. SE-EdS may be used to paint neutrinos into simulations in Fourier space, where its < 3% error and neutrinos' $\leq$ 3% matter fraction guarantees < 0.1% errors in the total matter density contrast, thereby including neutrino effects upon clustering at negligible computational cost. We quantify the approximation's accuracy; extend it to a broad range of cosmologies; and explore its correspondence with higher-order corrections to existing linear response schemes. A simple implementation is available online at https://codeberg.org/upadhye/SE-EdS .

title: On phases of 4d $Spin/SO$ Yang-Mills theories
summary: We study the low-temperature phase diagrams of $Spin(N)/SO(N)_\pm$ Yang-Mills theories as functions of the $θ$-parameter. In particular, for every even integer $N\geq 4$, we find a phase diagram consistent with the center/CP mixed anomaly, via the technique of mixed gauge theory. The resulting phase diagrams are in perfect agreement with the phase diagrams of $Spin(N)/SO(N)_\pm$ super Yang-Mills theory softly broken by a small gaugino mass. In the case of $Spin(4k)$ Yang-Mills for an integer $k\geq 2$, only two phases appear in the phase diagram, while in the $Spin(4)$ case the phase diagram contains four SPT phases protected by the $\mathbb{Z}_2\times \mathbb{Z}_2$ center symmetry. In the case of $Spin(4k+2)$ Yang-Mills for a positive integer $k$, the phase diagram contains four SPT phases protected by the $\mathbb{Z}_4$ center symmetry.

title: Coupled membrane response and horizon dissipation in four-dimensional Einstein-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet gravity
summary: We develop an action-based membrane paradigm for nonextremal, static, spherically symmetric black holes in four-dimensional Einstein-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet (EsGB) gravity, describing their interaction with external perturbations through an effective fluid membrane. We calculate the linear membrane responses to perturbations and use them to analyze the work done on the membrane and the energy absorbed by the horizon. Horizon energy absorption receives contributions from geometric shear and scalar interactions. The scalar contribution includes both direct work on the membrane and work associated with the induced horizon expansion. We then establish a balance relation between the integrated horizon absorption and the second-order change in Wald entropy between stationary horizon cuts. Applying this framework to slow dynamics near a simple turning point, we obtain the leading exponential growth or decay rate of spherically symmetric scalar perturbations without fitting a dynamical damping coefficient.

title: ReveaLLAGN 2: Exploring the Nuclear Gas and Stellar Kinematics of Nearby LLAGNs with JWST/NIRSpec IFU
comment: Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: Low-luminosity active galactic nuclei (LLAGN) represent the most common mode of black hole accretion in the local Universe, yet their nuclear structure, stellar and gas kinematics remain poorly constrained at parsec scales. We investigate the nuclear regions of eight nearby representative LLAGN, the ReveaLLAGN sample: M87, M104, M94, M81, NGC1052, NGC4258, NGC5128 and NGC4395. Using JWST/NIRSpec data, we probe the stellar, molecular hydrogen, hydrogen recombination, and high ionisation coronal lines kinematics and their spatial distribution, exploring how detectability and spatial distributions of these lines vary across different Eddington ratios. The stellar LOSV maps reveal a slowly rotating disk in the nuclei of all our targets, characterised by an anti-correlation with the h3 Gauss-Hermite moment. Across the sample, the stellar velocity dispersion rises toward the central black hole. Only in M104 and M94 does the velocity dispersion display a more intricate pattern that departs from a simple disk configuration, indicating the presence of multiple kinematic components in these galaxies. Across the sample, the gas distribution and kinematics exhibit rotation that is frequently decoupled from the stellar rotation, suggesting that the stellar gravitational potential is decoupled from the current accretion state. The gas kinematics are often visually aligned with the radio jet, presenting broader velocity dispersions along the jet direction. Line-ratio maps indicate that the dominant excitation mechanism is photoionisation by the central AGN, with mechanical heating from shocks becoming important only at higher Eddington ratios. Across the sample, we detect coronal lines in all LLAGN when using nuclear-aperture spectra, and we can obtain spatially resolved kinematics only in NGC5128 and NGC4395, the highest Eddington ratio sources.

title: Object-independent evaluation of small-data astronomical image classifiers: architecture, representation, and acquisition shortcuts
summary: Reported performance in small astronomical image datasets can reflect object reuse, field-of-view differences, acquisition settings, and catalogue-derived properties as well as astronomical morphology. We designed \dataset{} to measure these effects in a four-class task comprising galaxies, globular clusters, nebulae, and open clusters. The dataset contains 370 catalogue-supported physical objects, each represented by three Digitised Sky Survey FITS bands, and uses a group-constrained split of 222 training, 75 validation, and 73 test objects. We compared a custom CNN--Transformer trained from scratch with ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-50 and ViT-B/16 under an adaptive full-field representation, a common angular field, and two central-region-masked controls, using three fixed seeds. In the one-pass object-independent test, mean balanced accuracy on the adaptive view was $0.773\pm0.014$, $0.874\pm0.054$, and $0.866\pm0.023$ for the custom model, ResNet-50, and ViT-B/16, respectively. No primary architecture contrast rejected its null after Holm correction; ResNet-50 and ViT-B/16 differed by 0.007 balanced-accuracy points (95\% cluster-bootstrap interval $[-0.048,0.062]$). Controls based on acquisition and catalogue metadata reached 0.721--0.735, and central-region-masked adaptive views reached 0.731--0.800. These results demonstrate generalisation to unseen physical objects, but also show that image context, acquisition settings, and catalogue-derived object properties carry substantial class information. In this regime, high accuracy cannot be interpreted as evidence that a classifier learned target morphology, and the comparison does not isolate architecture from pretraining.

title: Hybrid Hadrons: Origins and Development
summary: Hybrid hadrons are states in which the gluonic field of the strong force contributes to the structure of the hadron. The idea arose in several places at nearly the same time in the mid-1970s because the advent of quantum chromodynamics made it clear that the carriers of the strong force are dynamical degrees of freedom. This resulted in the cavity resonators of the MIT bag model, in the vibrating strings inherited from the dual resonance model, in the Budapest membrane bag, and in a constituent-gluon potential model. The idea was subsequently developed in the early 1980s into a phenomenology capable of predicting masses, quantum numbers, and decay signatures. This article traces that history from the primary literature, giving close attention to dates of submission and to who first proposed what, and supplements the written record with recollections of many of the principal participants. It closes by surveying the current state of experimental, theoretical, and lattice research.

title: Cosmological Backreaction and the Separate Universe Conjecture: Dynamical volume partitioning of Newtonian cosmologies
summary: We provide a description of general Newtonian cosmologies for collisionless matter in terms of an exact and dynamical volume partitioning of global realizations of Newtonian models. Employing the formalism for the description of cosmological backreaction, an interaction between the inhomogeneities of the formation of structures in the Universe and their average properties can be analyzed. Our results can be regarded as a tool for many potential applications in the context of Newtonian simulations, but they also provide an exact way to assume analytical properties of the universe models on regional scales in conformity with global integral constraints on their average properties. We discuss approaches in relation to `separate Universe conjectures' in the literature and examine their consistency with the exact partitioning framework. In particular, using the Average Expansion Rate Approximation (AvERA) as an example, we show that identifying locally assigned Friedmannian rates with physical regional expansion rates is constrained by the global Newtonian 3-torus condition. Alternatively, when the simulation cells are interpreted as non-material control volumes, Reynolds transport introduces mass flux and flux-backreaction terms, so that their dynamics is not in general that of independent Friedmann domains. We also discuss the corresponding consistency conditions for stable clustering prescriptions.

title: Spectral flow in AdS$\mathbf{_3}$ revisited
comment: 66 pages, 6 figures. Includes ancillary Mathematica notebook
summary: We revisit an old idea that spectral flow in WZW models can be associated with certain $G$-bundles over a worldsheet. This allows us to introduce a novel method for computing correlators of spectrally-flowed vertex operators in WZW models with group $G$ and level $k$, by systematically computing the contribution from a network of line defects. Specialising to the case of $G=SL(2, \mathbb{R})$, as is relevant to AdS$_3$ string theory, we demonstrate that generic $n$-point functions of spectrally-flowed vertex operators at tree level can be rewritten in terms of an $(n+1)$-point function of $n$ unflowed vertex operators and one degenerate insertion. This is to be interpreted as an unflowed $n$-point function in an instanton background. Moreover, we conjecture that this $(n+1)$-point function can be recast as an $n$-point function of unflowed operators and we provide evidence for this. We demonstrate that the $(n+1)$-point function satisfies the same constraints from global spacetime conformal invariance as does an unflowed $n$-point function for a specific choice of spacetime coordinates that we determine. We verify that our results agree with bootstrap results in the literature. This provides the next step towards fully solving the $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ WZW model.

title: Missing solutions in scalar-Gauss-Bonnet gravity
summary: We discover novel neutron star solutions under scalar-Gauss-Bonnet (sGB) gravity which have been missed altogether in the existing literature. The complete solution space also reveals a new regularity condition that has to be satisfied by all scalarized stars. Certain scalarized branches of neutron star solutions under sGB gravity have long been known to abruptly terminate on stellar mass-radius diagrams at lower stellar radii, a phenomenon that has no counterpart in classical scalar-tensor theories. Such termination has been strongly suspected to be physical rather than a numerical artifact nevertheless, since sGB theories feature a regularity condition at the center of the star, which can prevent the existence of certain configurations. Motivated by the recently re-emerging phase-transition view of scalarization, we first predict that these terminated branches can reappear after a "gap." We confirm this by finding such reappearing branches, and also determine which parts of the theory parameter space are more amenable to such occurrences. We then show that the previously known central regularity condition cannot explain all the non-existing solutions in the gaps, which leads us to the discovery of a new, non-central, condition for the existence of scalarized neutron stars under sGB gravity.

title: DESI DR2 Results III: The Mass of the Milky Way
comment: This paper is a DESI Collaboration Key Project publication. 25+12 pages, 14+2 figures, 5+1 tables. Submitted to ApJ
summary: We present measurements of the mass of the Milky Way using distant halo stars selected from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) Data Release 2 (DR2). We apply four dynamical modeling methods to 10,036 RR Lyrae (RRL) and blue horizontal branch (BHB) stars with 6D phase space coordinates that span from $\sim$10 to 95 kpc from the Galactic center, the largest samples of their kind. All methods are applied to mock surveys based on cosmological simulations that include generating individual tracer stars, convolving their phase-space coordinates with DESI and Gaia DR3-like uncertainties, and tailored models of the survey selection functions. By comparing the performance on these mocks, we quantify how systematic biases from both methodology assumptions and galaxy disequilibrium impact each estimate. The mock-based systematics, which differ by method and tracer, are used to correct the individual estimates and to derive joint estimates using a rigorous formalism that accounts for per-method biases and residual correlations between methods. We obtain a joint estimate of the mass within 80 kpc to be $M(r < 80 \mathrm{\,kpc}) = 6.36^{+0.53}_{-0.48} \times 10^{11}$ M$_\odot$ and a virial mass estimate of $M_\mathrm{200c} = 1.19^{+0.14}_{-0.12} \times 10^{12}$ M$_\odot$, with similar results when combining only RRL-based or BHB-based measurements. These results provide a roadmap for future DESI efforts, as well as those in other spectroscopic surveys, to reliably constrain the mass of our Galaxy.

title: Adaptive Optics for the Extremely Large Telescope: overcoming Point Spread Function challenges with MORFEO
comment: 21 pages, 5 figures, published on New Astronomy on Aug 2026
summary: MORFEO is the multi-conjugate adaptive optics (MCAO) relay for the Extremely Large Telescope (ELT) of the European Southern Observatory. It combines the adaptive mirrors of the telescope (M4-M5) with two post-focal deformable mirrors to deliver a stable, diffraction-limited point spread function over a field approaching 1'. MORFEO senses the atmosphere using six sodium laser guide stars and up to three natural guide stars distributed across a $\sim$160'' technical field, enabling sky coverage levels of order 50% at the South Galactic Pole. Through its two gravity-invariant ports, MORFEO feeds the MICADO first-light imager and spectrograph with a corrected field of 51''and HARMONI, the high-angular resolution integral field spectrograph. SHARP, a concept for a multi-object near-infrared spectrograph at the ELT, adopts MORFEO as its reference MCAO architecture for evaluating achievable image quality and scientific performance. In this paper, we summarise the MCAO capabilities delivered by MORFEO, its optical quality, tomographic performance, stability of the corrected focal plane, and the accuracy of telemetry-based PSF reconstruction, and discuss their relevance for the development of SHARP and other wide-field spectroscopic concepts at the ELT.

title: Investigations on the low-lying $cccq\bar{q}$ resonances in a constituent quark model
summary: In present work, mass spectrum of the low-lying $cccq\bar{q}$ pentaquarks states with $q\bar{q}=u\bar{u}$, $d\bar{d}$ and $s\bar{s}$, are investigated employing a constituent quark model, within which the spin-dependent hyperfine interactions are taken to be the instanton-induced interaction and the one-gluon-exchange interaction, respectively. The model parameters are fixed by fitting the mass spectrum of the relative $q\bar{q}$ and $qqq$ traditional hadrons. The numerical results show that energies for all the obtained states in the two employed models are higher than corresponding meson-baryon channels, consequently, we roughly estimate strong decays of these states using a simple quark rearrangement model, the corresponding partial width ratios for different decay channels are presented.

title: Magnetohydrodynamics During Reheating
comment: 14+6 pages, 24 Figures, Comments and suggestions are most welcome
summary: Reheating is a crucial phase that connects inflation with the hot Big Bang Universe. During this phase, the nonlinear interactions among the inflaton, the radiation plasma, and the primordial magnetic fields can influence the subsequent evolution of cosmic structures we observe today. In this paper, we develop a multifluid framework to investigate the evolution of three dimensional nonlinear magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) during the non instantaneous reheating phase driven by the perturbative decay of the inflaton into the radiation plasma. For the present paper, we consider the simplest scenario where the inflaton field homogeneously injects energy into the radiation sector. We study the MHD evolution of the coupled inflaton radiation system during the reheating phase, including the evolution of their individual kinetic energies, the velocity perturbations, vorticity, magnetic fields, and gravitational waves. We find that homogeneous energy transfer from the inflaton to the radiation sector increases the radiation and kinetic energy densities but does not significantly amplify the initial magnetic field perturbations. Consequently, the magnetic spectrum remains largely unchanged with respect to the instantaneous reheating scenario, while the velocity perturbations undergo a scale redistribution that affects the resulting GW spectrum. Our results demonstrate the importance of nonlinear multifluid MHD dynamics in understanding the evolution of primordial fields during reheating and provide a framework for exploring more realistic scenarios involving inhomogeneous decay processes and detailed thermalization effects.

title: A dynamical Einstein-Proca-dilaton holographic model and exotic hybrid meson resonances
summary: A fully dynamical Einstein-Proca-dilaton (EPD) holographic model is developed for the exotic $J^{PC}=1^{-+}$ hybrid meson, incorporating the backreaction of the massive vector field dual to the hybrid current in the bulk. Solving the coupled EPD system yields a self-consistent gravitational background and the mass spectrum of hybrid resonances. While the soft-wall limit reproduces linear Regge behavior, the inclusion of backreaction yields quantitative shifts that improve agreement with experimental candidates. The finite-temperature regime is approached by studying black hole thermodynamics and spectral functions across the confinement-deconfinement transition, fixing the Hawking-Page temperature to $T_c \sim 150 \, \mathrm{MeV}$. Unlike non-backreacted AdS/QCD models, the dynamical background predicts a strong suppression of hybrid states already near the onset of deconfinement. These results demonstrate that gravitational backreaction has measurable consequences for both vacuum spectroscopy and in-medium properties of exotic hybrid mesons, emphasizing the relevance of a dynamical self-consistent approach in AdS/QCD.

title: Metric reconstruction in a Bondi-like gauge
summary: Metric perturbations obtained from a Hertz potential in an ingoing radiation gauge (IRG) generically grow in an outgoing coordinate $r$ at future null infinity, and are therefore not asymptotically flat in the Bondi sense. Hollands and Toomani showed that this growth can be removed, within the Green--Hollands--Zimmerman (GHZ) framework, by an IRG-compatible ``residual'' gauge transformation together with a carefully chosen choice of the undetermined integration ``constants'' of the Hertz potential. In this work we turn that proof into a practical algorithm. We show that this entire completion is generated by a single ``Held Master Scalar'' (HMS), which can be thought of as a function on future null infinity. The HMS is obtained from the leading asymptotic piece of the $0$-Weyl scalar through a Teukolsky--Starobinsky inversion. We give explicit formulas for the four integration constants of the Hertz potential associated with the $0$-Weyl scalar, and for the residual gauge vector in terms of the HMS, thereby bringing the metric perturbation into a Bondi-like gauge. In Schwarzschild the entire construction is diagonal in $(\ell, m)$-modes and every completion field is available in closed form; in Kerr the construction is tri-diagonal. We have numerically implemented the full scheme in $(\ell,m)$ and in $m$-modes, including the corrector piece of the GHZ framework. We illustrate our scheme numerically for a point-particle on a circular orbit in a puncture scheme in Schwarzschild and in Kerr, by demonstrating the Bondi-like fall-off. We also find agreement with the known Detweiler redshift computations in Schwarzschild and Kerr. Our method directly gives the Bondi news, mass-, and angular momentum aspects, for which we give exemplary results in Kerr.

title: Mock catalogues for the DESI DR2 Milky Way mass modeling effort
comment: This paper is a DESI Collaboration Key Project publication. 13+4 pages, 9+0 figures, 0+2 tables. Submitted to The Open Journal of Astrophysics, comments welcome
summary: The Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) survey is an ongoing campaign to obtain millions of spectra, including for stars within the Milky Way. One of DESI's Key Projects for its second data release (DR2) is to measure the mass of the Milky Way using a variety of techniques applied to six-dimensional kinematics of distant halo stars. We present mock surveys generated from the Auriga cosmological simulations (AuriDESI) that are used to validate these techniques in several companion studies. The AuriDESI tracer catalogues are tailored to reflect key features of the DR2 Key Project dataset, including the selection of RR Lyrae and blue horizontal branch stars, uncertainties on line-of-sight velocities and proper motions, and variation in observational completeness within the survey footprint. We discuss how well the resulting AuriDESI tracer catalogues compare to their observed DESI counterparts, including suggesting improvements that can be generalized to similar mock survey efforts within the community. The AuriDESI tracer catalogues are publicly available on Zenodo.

title: Tracking turbulence for wind-driven halo removal using MagAO-X pyramid wavefront sensor images
comment: 59 pages, 11 figures, 6 tables; Accepted for publication in SPIE JATIS
summary: The wind-driven halo (WDH) is a persistent, low spatial frequency noise artifact that arises due to the servo-lag error inherent to all adaptive optics (AO) instruments. Spatial filtering may be employed to overcome this artifact, however, filtering out the WDH while simultaneously preserving signal from an extended astrophysical object of interest is exceptionally challenging. Additionally, since the WDH changes in intensity and position angle through an observation, data-driven algorithms (e.g., KLIP) that are commonly used to subtract the starlight need to be overly-aggressive to remove both the static and dynamic noise components. Since wavefront sensors (WFSs) continuously track the closed-loop residual wavefront error, WFS telemetry presents the ideal resource for combating this type of noise artifact through postprocessing. Using archival WFS telemetry from MagAO-X, which is the "extreme" AO instrument for the 6.5-meter Magellan-Clay telescope, we demonstrate a novel workflow for WDH reconstruction and removal in individual coronagraphic science images. MagAO-X is equipped with a pyramid WFS capable of recording wavefront telemetry at a high-cadence which is saved during data acquisition. Given this, we detail how our WFS data processing pipeline, windsoCC, cross-correlates the recorded closed-loop wavefront to measure the wind vectors of several turbulent layers of the atmosphere above Las Campanas Observatory. We then make use of the wind parameters learned through windsoCC to reconstruct the WDH footprint by leveraging a parametric model. Notably, we demonstrate a dramatic improvement in object recovery using on-sky MagAO-X images of the disk around HR 4796A at visible wavelengths.

title: From lattice QCD thermodynamics to an effective quasiparticle description of gluonic matter at finite temperature
summary: We develop a lattice-constrained quasiparticle description of pure SU(3) Yang--Mills matter at finite temperature. The temperature-dependent effective gluon quasiparticle mass is determined from the lattice entropy density over $0.70\leq T/T_c\leq5$. It is interpreted as an effective thermal parameter encoding medium modifications of gluonic excitations, rather than as a physical gluon mass. With this mass fixed, we reconstruct the background contribution required for thermodynamic consistency, using a single pressure-normalization condition. The resulting pressure, energy density, entropy density, interaction measure, and squared speed of sound are then compared with available lattice results. Near $T_c$, the rapid variation of the effective mass is accompanied by a pronounced maximum in the interaction measure at $T/T_c\simeq1.09$, a strong suppression of the squared speed of sound, and a maximum in the background contribution. These correlated features characterize the substantial departure from conformal behavior in the transition region. At higher temperatures, the interaction measure decreases and the squared speed of sound approaches the conformal limit. We also examine the energy-per-excitation ratio $E/n_g$, which has a minimum of approximately $964~\mathrm{MeV}$ at $T/T_c\simeq1.21$. This ratio provides a measure of the excitation scale within the quasiparticle description. Overall, our results show how lattice thermodynamics can be mapped onto an effective gluonic excitation spectrum while maintaining thermodynamic consistency.

title: Shining LIMelight into the dark: Probing Dark matter - baryon interactions with Line Intensity Mapping
comment: v1: 28 pages, 15 figures. Comments are welcome. For a short video explaining the work, please see:https://youtu.be/JQtsGuOoQNM?si=zlQhGX9KURA0_Ezr
summary: Line-intensity mapping (LIM) is an emerging technique for probing both the astrophysics of galaxy formation and the cosmological evolution of large-scale structure. We investigate, for the first time, its potential as a probe of dark matter-baryon (DM-$b$) interactions using the upcoming Carbon Monoxide Mapping Array Project (COMAP) surveys, COMAP-EoR (Epoch of Reionization) and COMAP-ERA (Expanded Reionization Array). Elastic scattering of dark matter (DM) with baryons, i.e., protons ($p$) and electrons ($e$), exchange momentum and heat with the DM, suppressing structure formation and leaving characteristic signatures in the linear matter power spectrum. These effects propagate to the LIM power spectrum (PS) and voxel intensity distribution (VID). We consider momentum-transfer cross sections $σ^{χb}_{T,n}=σ^{χb}_{n}v^n$, with $n=0,-2,$ and $-4$, corresponding to contact, electric dipole-moment-like, and Coulomb-like interactions, respectively. Using Fisher forecasts, we obtain the projected sensitivities to $σ^{χb}_{n}$ from the PS and VID. Our VID-only forecasts combining the 16 and 30 GHz observed bands yield stronger sensitivities than existing cosmological limits for $n=-2$ and $n=-4$ for sub-GeV DM masses. We also explore the potential of combining the PS and VID to probe these interactions. Our study highlights LIM as a complementary probe of DM models alongside other astrophysical, cosmological, and terrestrial searches.

title: Striped phases of N=4 SYM at finite density
summary: We construct spatially modulated phases of strongly coupled $\mathcal N=4$ supersymmetric Yang--Mills theory at finite $R$-charge density. Compactification on a three-torus and unequal background charges isolate an unstable charge-density mode. Its static threshold seeds a nonlinear branch of striped black branes in the STU model. The striped states have higher entropy than homogeneous states with the same energy and conserved charges. They connect continuously to the homogeneous branch, with an entropy excess that begins at fourth order in the modulation amplitude. These solutions provide a candidate endpoint of the charge-transport instability.

title: Constraining Lorentz Invariance Violation via Precision Atomic Spectroscopy
summary: This paper investigates Lorentz violation arising from quantum gravity effects in electronic and muonic hydrogen atoms. The violation is modeled through a modified dispersion relation parameterized by a dimensionless coefficient $ξ$ and suppressed by the Planck scale. Using high-precision spectroscopic data and a chi-squared fitting procedure that carefully accounts for theoretical uncertainties in the Rydberg constant and the proton radius, the analysis yields a 95% confidence level constraint $ξ\in [-14.3,\; 1.37] \times 10^5$. The mass scaling of the effect reveals two distinct regimes: for the lowest-order deformation, the heavy nucleus amplifies the signal, while for higher-order corrections, the lepton dominates the sensitivity. These bounds approach Planck-scale sensitivity using the simplest atomic systems, thereby circumventing ambiguities inherent in more complex quantum systems.

title: Constraining the Milky Way Mass profile with data driven distribution function using DESI DR2 halo stars
comment: 23 pages, 11 figures. This paper is a DESI Collaboration Key Project publication
summary: We employ a novel data-driven dynamical modeling method, the empirical distribution function (emPDF), to constrain the Milky Way mass profile using a large sample of halo stars from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument Milky Way Survey (DESI MWS). The method does not assume any functional form of the tracer distribution. Deviations from the steady-state assumption and the effects of observational errors are further tested and calibrated using a number of realistic mock observations (AuriDESI). Applying the calibrated method to two classes of tracers in DESI, we derive a best-constrained virial mass and concentration of $\log M_\mathrm{200c}/M_{\odot}=12.05_{-0.12}^{+0.21}(_{-0.18}^{+0.26})$ and $\log c_\mathrm{200c}=1.20_{-0.16}^{+0.11}(_{-0.24}^{+0.20})$ for BHBs. For RR Lyrae stars we derive $\log M_\mathrm{200c}/M_{\odot}=12.15_{-0.14}^{+0.22}(_{-0.19}^{+0.26})$ and $\log c_\mathrm{200c}=1.16_{-0.12}^{+0.09}(_{-0.18}^{+0.16})$. The uncertainties quoted outside and within brackets are statistical and total errors including systematic errors calibrated from AuriDESI, respectively. The two tracer populations provide overall consistent measurements of the MW halo mass profile. Combining the halo star constraints with the independent constraint from satellite dynamics, we derive a robust and precise final measurement of the MW halo parameters of $\log M_\mathrm{200c}/M_{\odot}=12.12_{-0.05}^{+0.05}(_{-0.04}^{+0.06})$ and $\log c_\mathrm{200c}=1.16_{-0.03}^{+0.05}(_{-0.07}^{+0.05})$, with correlation coefficients of $ρ=-0.90(-0.54)$.

title: Quiescent galaxies at cosmic noon: from individual element abundances to star formation histories
comment: 8 pages, 2 figures, published on New Astronomy
summary: Understanding the formation and early evolution of massive quiescent galaxies is crucial for a complete picture of galaxy formation in a cosmological context. Such a comprehensive picture can be obtained through measurements of individual elemental abundances, which encode the timescales and physical conditions of their star-formation and assembly histories. While extensive work at low and intermediate redshift has revealed strong correlations between stellar mass, metallicity, and abundance ratios, studies at z ~ 2-3 remain extremely limited. Their faintness and compactness make medium-resolution near-infrared spectroscopy for detailed chemical analysis extremely challenging. We present a science case to measure full elemental abundance patterns in a representative sample of massive quiescent galaxies at cosmic noon, exploiting rest-frame optical absorption features. We show that deriving robust stellar population constraints for these systems requires spectra with S/N ~ 20 per resolution element, together with a spatial resolution comparable to their ~ 0.1 arcsec sizes. We show that such requirements can only be met with a 40m class telescope equipped with a powerful adaptive optics system. In this context, SHARP-NEXUS, in combination with MORFEO-MCAO capabilities, emerges as the only viable ELT instrument capable of enabling this science, providing both the sensitivity and angular resolution needed. Although massive quiescent galaxies are rare at these redshifts, their study can efficiently exploit the instrument's multiplexing by targeting galaxy overdensities and coordinating with surveys of star-forming galaxies. Such synergistic strategies, proven feasible in high-redshift clusters and by multiplex-sharing facilities like 4MOST, would allow SHARP-NEXUS to open a new window on the chemical enrichment of the earliest massive galaxies.

title: What Does Precision Spectroscopy Actually Constrain about X17 Couplings?
summary: Can precision spectroscopy disentangle the individual couplings of the X17 boson? Within a leading one-body model, we combine electronic and muonic spectroscopy of hydrogen, deuterium and helium with lepton magnetic moments. We show that hydrogen-deuterium comparisons can lose neutron sensitivity through cancellations, while the combined observables restore generic local identifiability without guaranteeing finite individual bounds. The unrestricted fit admits formally unbounded nucleon-coupling directions, some of which violate the assumptions underlying the physical model. Finite-coupling tests nevertheless reveal statistically compatible solutions, with bounds dependent on nuclear responses and physical assumptions. Our results establish what precision measurements genuinely constrain and what additional information is required to extract meaningful limits on X17 couplings.

title: Quasi-Normal Modes and thermalization in integrable Quantum Field Theories from the Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz
summary: We propose a Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz (TBA) approach for describing thermalization in integrable quantum field theories. The exponential damping and oscillations when approaching thermal equilibrium can be understood as the analogs of quasi-normal mode (QNM) frequencies of black hole perturbations within the framework of holography. Holographic intuitions and some general properties of thermal Green's functions motivate the existence of such a TBA formulation, as well as lead to the imposition of a nonstandard analytical structure on the QNM TBA, while comparison with integrable form-factor expansions fixes the remaining ingredients. We conjecture the QNM TBA to be equivalent to performing an all-order resummation of secular terms in a thermal form factor expansion of retarded 2-point correlation functions. We compare the predictions with tensor network simulations of the E8 deformation of Ising CFT at nonzero temperature. We conjecture that the QNM TBA framework should also be applicable for describing out-of-equilibrium approach to Generalized Hydrodynamics (GHD).

title: A Geometric No-Go Theorem for Regular Black Holes in Scalar-Tensor Theories
summary: Perturbative instabilities generically puzzles singularity-free spacetimes, including non-singular bounce, traversible wormholes and regular black holes (RBHs). Can the scalar-tensor (ST) theories that stabilize the first two also stabilize RBHs? We show that the answer is no for static, spherically symmetric RBHs supported by a radial scalar field within a broad class of ST theories. In any RBHs with two-horizon structure, the ratio of the longitudinal scale to the sphere radius must attain an interior maximum. The proper-time derivative of that ratio is associated to the squared propagation speed of odd-parity tensor perturbations by the background field equations in a broad class of scalar-tensor theories. A Lorentzian odd-tensor cone then requires a local minimum instead of a maximum. This conflicts indicate a geometric no-go theorem, covering a broad class of ST theories including spatially covariant gravity, Horndeski theory, quadratic GLPV, DHOST, and U-DHOST theories, and their admissible disformal extensions. Viable RBHs therefore require relaxing at least one geometric or dynamical assumption.

title: A distribution-function estimate of the Milky Way mass profile from outer halo stars in DESI DR2
comment: This paper is a DESI Collaboration Key Project publication. To be submitted to OJAp. 23 pages, 11 figures
summary: We present measurements of the Milky Way mass using blue horizontal-branch (BHB) and RR Lyrae (RRL) stars from the second data release of DESI (DR2), covering its first three years of operations. We employ 279 BHBs and 213 RRLs at $\sim\!50$--$80$\,kpc from the Galactic center, selected from catalogs roughly twice as large as those of DESI DR1, used in our previous mass measurement. We apply the Galactic Mass Estimator (GME), a hierarchical Bayesian framework that assumes power-law forms for the potential and the tracer density, and accounts for distance and velocity uncertainties. Validating the method on 24 AuriDESI mock catalogs (six Auriga halos at four viewing angles), we find that it overestimates the enclosed mass by $\sim\!15\%$ at 80\,kpc, and correct our results accordingly. We obtain $M(<80\,{\rm kpc}) = 0.64^{+0.06}_{-0.06}$ and $0.53^{+0.05}_{-0.05} \times 10^{12}\,M_\odot$ for BHBs and RRLs, respectively, while including Sagittarius stream stars lowers these masses by $\sim\!10$\%. Extrapolating to 100\,kpc, we obtain $M(<100\,{\rm kpc}) = 0.74^{+0.07}_{-0.07}$ and $0.62^{+0.06}_{-0.07} \times 10^{12}\,M_\odot$, and anchoring an NFW halo to our GME constraints at 65\,kpc yields virial masses of $M_{200} = 1.12^{+0.14}_{-0.12}$ and $0.89^{+0.11}_{-0.10} \times 10^{12}\,M_\odot$. BHBs yield systematically higher masses than RRLs across the full radial range, reflecting the impact of tracer choice even within a single method. This work is part of a wider DESI DR2 Key Project effort to measure the Milky Way mass and constrain systematics arising from different samples and methodologies.

title: Probing Lorentz Symmetry Violation via Hadroproduction in Electroweak Pair Annihilation
comment: The manuscript includes 10 pages and 2 figures
summary: The violation of Lorentz symmetry is anticipated in some theories beyond the Standard Model so various processes have been studied to search for the effects of Lorentz symmetry violation (LSV). High energy collision experiments provide a suitable environment where Lorentz symmetry breaking can be examined. In this work, we study the effect of Lorentz-violating terms on the hadron production process from pair annihilation, including a vectorial nonminimal coupling between the fermions and gauge fields in the Electroweak sector. To be specific, we study the effect of CPT-odd nonminimal Lorentz symmetry violating couplings on the production of bottom flavored mesons through pair annihilation in the Electroweak theory, i.e., $e^+e^-\to q\bar{q}\to B+Jets$. Considering the available data and the analytical result for the tree-level cross section $σ^{LO}(e^+e^-\to B+Jets)$ in the presence of LSV terms, we determine an upper bound on the purely time-like background 4-vector as strict as $\le 10^{-3} GeV^{-1}$, in agreement with previous works on similar Lorentz violating couplings.

title: The PAU Survey: Self-supervised image denoising for flux-preserving photometry
summary: Context. Deep photometric surveys increasingly rely on low signal-to-noise imaging, where noise affects source detection, flux measurements, photometric redshifts, and sample selection. Self-supervised denoising methods are attractive because they do not require ground-truth images, but applying them to quantitative photometry requires controlling the flux biases they may introduce. Aims. We evaluate and improve Noise2Void (N2V) for denoising real astronomical images, focusing on preserving fluxes, reducing photometric scatter, and retaining the main source features across a wide magnitude range. Methods. We use real observations from the Physics of the Accelerating Universe Survey (PAUS) together with PAUS-like simulated images. We show that standard N2V systematically underestimates galaxy fluxes, especially for faint galaxies. To mitigate this bias, we add a bounded-output layer that limits large negative outputs, and fine-tune the model with low-rank adaptation (LoRA) and two flux-aware loss terms that preserve the flux scale and improve repeated-exposure flux consistency. Results. For PAUS galaxies with 22 <= i_AB < 23 in the NB645 band, the standard N2V flux-ratio distribution peaks far below unity, while the bounded-output model restores it close to the original PAUS flux scale. The flux-aware LoRA fine-tuning reduces the width of the repeated-exposure flux-difference distribution to sigma_68 = 0.529 in NB645, an effective 47% reduction in random flux scatter relative to the original PAUS uncertainty scale, while keeping the median flux ratio close to unity. Conclusions. Denoising methods for astronomical surveys must be evaluated with photometric diagnostics, not image-quality metrics alone. With flux-aware modifications, self-supervised denoising can be adapted to low-SNR survey images while preserving the flux information needed for quantitative analysis.

title: Higher Integrability, Generalized Symmetries, and Partially Topological Field Theories
summary: We exhibit a classical link between higher Lax integrability and generalized symmetries in a non-Lorentzian higher semi-holomorphic Chern--Simons theory on $M\times\mathbb CP^1$. The equations of motion determine a spectrally dependent flat higher connection on $M$ whose Laurent coefficients organise an infinite hierarchy of conserved quantities. We construct a spectral family of classical $(d_M-2)$-form symmetry line defects associated with the Lax connection, establish an action-preserving deformation law, and exhibit suitable gauge-invariant probes on which the induced transformations act nontrivially.

title: Quasinormal modes of charged de Sitter black holes and strong cosmic censorship in conformal Killing gravity
summary: The strong cosmic censorship conjecture argues that the future evolution of the spacetime should be predictable from the initial data. However, within the framework of general relativity, some counterexamples to the conjecture have been found, especially for de Sitter spacetime. Spurred by challenges to the validity of the strong cosmic censorship conjecture, we extend such investigations to conformal Killing gravity, a promising candidate beyond Einstein's theory. Considering neutral massless scalar perturbations for charged de Sitter black hole, we not only shed light on the quasinormal mode spectrum, but also clarify whether the modifications from conformal Killing gravity and nonlinear electrodynamics can rescue the strong cosmic censorship conjecture, and further investigate how characteristic parameters affect its validity. As the first instance for investigating the conjecture in the framework of conformal Killing gravity, this paper reports some unexpected findings.

title: Identifying Compact Object Candidates using Gaia DR3 Astrometric Accelerations and Jerks
comment: 16 pages, 7 figures, submitted to AAS journals, comments welcome
summary: Gaia Data Release 3 (DR3) provides astrometric measurements for more than a billion sources, hundreds of thousands of which have non-single-star astrometric solutions that indicate deviations from linear proper motion. Although sources with orbital solutions have been extensively inspected for compact objects via the astrometric mass function, two other solution types--the 7-parameter constant-acceleration solutions characterized by $\dot{\mathbfμ}$, and the 9-parameter variable-acceleration solutions characterized by $\dot{\mathbfμ}$ and $\ddot{\mathbfμ}$--have not been as carefully explored. In this work, we develop a methodology for selecting sources within the Gaia DR3 9-parameter non-single-star astrometric solutions that are most likely to host massive compact companions. We assume that a source is the luminous star in a binary orbit around a dark object and derive analytic expressions for the sky-projected accelerations and jerks for three binary populations with different orbit approximations: inclined eccentric, face-on eccentric, and face-on circular. Using POSYDON, we develop a fourth, more realistic population of binaries, each consisting of a luminous star and a black hole. For each population, we address observational biases using gaiamock and select only the systems it fits with a 9-parameter solution. We find that binaries likely to host massive compact companions can be identified from the characteristic joint astrometric accelerations and jerks exhibited by the luminous stars, despite 9-parameter fits under-constraining full orbits. Finally, to illustrate the utility of our approach, we analyze a historical object of interest, HD 12871, and examine 9-parameter fits of Gaia BH3-like binaries.

title: A Duality Model in Which Dual QCD Becomes Hydrodynamics
summary: Revisiting a duality model in which dual QCD becomes hydrodynamics, or the dual gluon is a fluid, allows us to understand some of the mysteries of QCD, such as the behavior of the quark--gluon plasma (QGP) as a perfect fluid and gluon saturation in the structure function at high energies. This old-fashioned duality converts the gluon action into hydrodynamics described by the 2-form stream function $W^a_{μν}$ with eight colors. All interactions then become current--current interactions of the Nambu--Jona-Lasinio type. The resulting theory admits a strong-coupling expansion about the fluid. This can provide a third method to supplement perturbative QCD and lattice QCD.

title: CosmoVerse Data Challenge: How Tip of the Red Giant Branch Analysis Choices Shape the Inferred Hubble Constant
summary: Tip of the red giant branch (TRGB)-based determinations of the Hubble constant ($H_0$), the current expansion rate of the Universe, depend on choices made in selecting and analyzing stellar photometry and in assembling the sample of calibrator galaxies hosting Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia). The CosmoVerse Data Challenge invites participants to analyze public photometric catalogs within a shared distance-ladder framework, opening each step of the measurement to the community and testing how these choices propagate into $H_0$. Participants independently selected photometric catalogs, galaxies, and TRGB measurement settings, while using a common SN Ia compilation and fitting procedure to convert distances into $H_0$. Supported by public notebooks and a training school, the challenge received 26 submissions from 22 participants. All submissions used the same analysis notebook, many participants were trainees at the school, and the true galaxy distances are unknown; the results therefore characterize the sensitivity of the submissions to analysis and sample-selection choices and are not a combined determination of $H_0$ or an estimate of the systematic uncertainty in published TRGB measurements. The inferred $H_0$ values have a median of $77.10\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ and a standard deviation of $7.38\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ $(5.11\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ for the scaled median absolute deviation), $\sim 3.4$ $(\sim 2.4)$ times the typical quoted uncertainty of a submission. Differences in the measured tip of the anchor galaxy NGC 4258 add a coherent shift in the distance scale. The challenge shows how different choices within a common framework can produce substantially different values of $H_0$, and provides an open basis for tracing these differences and for making datasets and tools more transparent and accessible.

title: Form Factors in AdS from the Worldsheet
summary: We study AdS form factors describing closed strings scattering off D-branes. Assuming that these form factors admit worldsheet integral representations in terms of multiple polylogarithms, we determine their leading curvature corrections around the flat-space limit by matching their pole structure to CFT data. We focus on two examples of defects in 4d $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM: a $\frac{1}{2}$-BPS 't Hooft loop, dual to a D1 brane, and a pair of giant gravitons, dual to a D3 brane. For the 't Hooft loop, the worldsheet bootstrap completely fixes the form factor, and the result passes nontrivial checks from supersymmetric localization. For the giant gravitons, the bootstrap initially leaves five free coefficients, one of which can be fixed using localization. Remarkably, imposing instead that no new operators appear in the defect channel at this order fixes all five coefficients and reproduces the localization constraint. Under this additional assumption, we therefore obtain a unique D3-brane form factor, with supersymmetric localization providing an independent check.

title: Probing black bounce spacetime through mass accretion rate
summary: We study steady, spherically symmetric accretion of a collisionless kinetic gas onto a compact object described by the Simpson--Visser (SV) metric, a one-parameter regularization of the Schwarzschild spacetime. Using the standard relativistic Vlasov formalism, we adopt boundary conditions at a finite injection radius $R$ and compute the mass accretion rate $\dot{M}$ for Vlasov gas with both monoenergetic and Maxwell--Jüttner distribution functions. Throughout the computation, we also take into account the influence of particle's angular momentum. We carefully investigate the influence of the black bounce parameter on the mass accretion rate $\dot{M}$. By expanding accretion rate in terms of bounce parameter $a$, we found that the leading-order correction appears at quadratic order in $a$. This work extends the Vlasov accretion framework to a broader class of spherically symmetric spacetimes and quantifies the impact of the geometric modification on the accretion flow. In particular, since the shadows of the SV and Schwarzschild black holes are degenerate, comparing their mass accretion rates may offer a complementary probe for distinguishing these geometries in future astrophysical observations.

title: Revisiting the Stellar-Dynamical Mass of the Central Black Hole in NGC 3227
summary: We present a new stellar-dynamical mass for the supermassive black hole in the nearby Seyfert galaxy NGC 3227. We determined the line-of-sight velocity distributions of stars in the nuclear region of NGC 3227 using archival spatially-resolved $K$-band spectra obtained with NIFS at Gemini Observatory. The surface brightness profile of the galaxy is described by four components, measured from a WFC3 F547M image from the Hubble Space Telescope. We constructed dynamical models using the Schwarzschild orbit-superposition method implemented in the open-source code $\texttt{FORSTAND}$. We find a best-fit black hole mass of $M_{\mathrm{BH}}$=$(1.2\pm0.5) \times 10^7$ $M_{\odot}$. This mass is consistent with a previous mass from R. I. Davies et al. based on stellar dynamics using orbit-based modeling, but our results make use of higher signal-to-noise data from which the higher-order moments of the stellar LOSVDs are constrained, thus providing a more precise $M_{\mathrm{BH}}$. Our result is also consistent with the $M_{\mathrm{BH}}$ constraint from velocity-resolved reverberation mapping reported by M. C. Bentz et al.. And while our best-fit mass is slightly smaller than the mass constraint from gas-dynamical modeling reported by E. K. S. Hicks & M. A. Malkan (after scaling to the same adopted distance), they are within 2$σ$ of each other. Direct comparisons of black hole masses from different techniques are rare but crucial to ensure all black hole masses are on the same scale, and to identify and minimize the uncertainties and possible sources of bias associated with each technique.

title: Quantum field theory treatment of the spin-flavor precession of Dirac neutrinos with diagonal magnetic moments
comment: 10 pages in Revtex, 1 pdf figure; contribution to the proceedings of the 20th Workshop on High Energy Spin Physics (Dubna, Russia, September 7-11, 2026)
summary: We apply the quantum field theory (QFT) approach to describe the spin-flavor precession of Dirac neutrinos. The magnetic moments matrix of these neutrinos is taken to be diagonal in the mass basis. Neutrino mass eigenstates are considered to be virtual particles in the QFT approach. The neutrino contribution to the matrix element of the overall process, which includes the emission, the propagation and the detection of neutrinos, is contained in the propagators of massive neutrinos. Using the recently derived propagator of a massive neutrino, which exactly accounts for the magnetic moment interaction, we derive the transition probability of the process $ν_{e\mathrm{L}}\toν_{μ\mathrm{L}}$ under the influence of a magnetic field. The result is compared with the prediction of the standard quantum mechanical (QM) approach. We briefly discuss the possibility to derive the QFT corrections to the QM expressions.

title: The Start Time of Ringdown
summary: We determine the convergence of quasi-normal modes sums for a point-particle plunging into a Schwarzschild black hole. While a dynamical amplitude model reproduces the waveform after the particle crosses the bounce radius, a constant amplitude sum converges only after the start time $t_S$, which corresponds to the advanced time at which the particle hits the central singularity. For a plunge from the ISCO, $t_S \simeq 9.4 M$ after the peak of the $22$ mode. After $t_S$, dynamical and constant amplitudes models are equivalent; our analysis also implies that any "direct wave" must reduce to the late-time tail after $t_S$.

title: 5-brane webs and generalised symmetries
summary: 5-brane webs provide a powerful geometric description of five-dimensional quantum field theories, encoding data such as symmetries and dualities. Although the extraction of continuous 0-form symmetries from these systems is well understood, their higher-form symmetries have received less attention. We develop a microscopic prescription for determining 1-form symmetries directly from 5-brane webs. BPS Wilson lines are represented by configurations of D3-branes and $(p,q)$ strings, while their screening by local operators is realised through string junctions, Higgsing, and Hanany-Witten transitions. For webs without orientifold planes, this construction reproduces the Smith normal form prescription based on asymptotic 7-brane charges. We extend the analysis to webs containing O7- and O5- planes. For O7$^-$-planes, the resolved 7-brane charges can be incorporated into the Smith normal form, whereas for O7$^+$-planes we propose an effective charge prescription and test it in both Lagrangian and non-Lagrangian examples. For webs with O5-planes, configurations of half-D3-branes reproduce the centre symmetries of Spin gauge theories and their breaking by matter. Crucially, we find that the 1-form symmetry of an O5-plane system is not determined by asymptotic data alone, but can depend on the local structure of the brane configuration near the orientifold.

title: Dipolar boson stars as static two-body systems: an effective-one-body description
summary: Dipolar boson stars consist of two scalar-field lumps held in static equilibrium by the balance between gravitational attraction and scalar repulsion. The repulsion stems from a $π$ phase difference between the harmonically varying complex scalar field sourcing each lump. We construct sequences of these configurations numerically and describe them analytically as bound states of two boson stars within the effective-one-body (EOB) formalism. We map the EOB potential previously derived for the scattering of two boson stars onto an energy-dependent Schwarzschild-like radial potential. We find that the EOB-based analytical prediction for the binding energy of the system agrees remarkably well with the numerical values. The analytical prediction for the critical gravitational coupling beyond which no static equilibrium exists is also consistent with the numerical results.

title: The impact of Population III stars on the elemental enrichment of ultra-faint galaxies in the FIRE-3 zoom-in simulations
summary: The observed stellar mass-metallicity relation for ultra-faint galaxies in the Local Group (LG) is in tension with many theoretical predictions, suggesting the need for modified or additional channels of elemental enrichment at low metallicities. We present a suite of FIRE-3 cosmological baryonic zoom-in simulations of isolated ultra-faint galaxies run to z=0 (maximum baryonic resolution ~ 30 Msun, 0.1 pc) and LMC-mass environments (maximum baryonic resolution ~ 110 Msun, 0.5 pc), with different sub-grid models for Population III stars. Under our Pop. III model(s), star particles forming below a critical metallicity Z_crit represent an initial mass function (IMF) consisting of only massive stars (8-100 Msun). We examine how various stellar feedback processes impact the star formation histories (SFHs) and elemental abundances of ultra-faint galaxies. We find that our Pop. III model variants introduce an effective metallicity floor in ultra-faints at z=0, at Z_floor ~ 1e-5 Zsun to 1e-3 Zsun or [Fe/H]_floor ~ -7 to -5 depending on the model. However, simply including the Pop. III model does not systematically guarantee that all (or even most) ultra-faints enrich up to [Fe/H] ~ -2.5 to fully resolve the tension with the observed mass-metallicity relation, even though we obtain some galaxies at that level. Crucially, the ultra-faints that do enrich in [Fe/H] to this level observed in the LG have extended SFHs after Pop. III enrichment and significant iron enrichment from white dwarf (Type Ia) supernovae, indicating that iron enrichment from Pop. III alone is not sufficient. We also examine the ways in which early-time Pop. III feedback impacts the metallicity distributions and [Mg/Fe] abundance ratios in ultra-faint galaxies, and make a prediction for the stellar mass - [Mg/H] metallicity relation from our simulations.

title: Heavy quarkonium spin transport in a hot medium
summary: We investigate the in-medium spin transport of heavy quarkonium using an open-quantum-system approach based on potential nonrelativistic QCD. We express the heavy quarkonium dilepton decay angular distribution in terms of late-time quarkonium spin-dependent distribution functions. Working in the quantum-optical regime, where the inverse quarkonium size is much larger than the binding energy and the binding energy is comparable to or larger than the medium temperature $T$, we derive a spin-dependent quantum master equation incorporating both dissociation and regeneration, followed by the corresponding projected semiclassical Boltzmann equations. At leading order in the coupling, we retain the recoil corrections of relative order $T/M$ that contribute to the leading spin-dependent collision kernel. Here $M$ denotes the heavy-quark mass. At zeroth order in fluid gradients, we show that the relative motion between quarkonium and the medium supplies the leading anisotropy, while spin-chromomagnetic and spin-orbit interactions both contribute to the leading nonzero spin-alignment kernel. As an exploratory phenomenological application, we also estimate the medium-induced polarization parameter $λ_θ$ of bottomonium $Υ(1\text{S})$ using a simplified rate equation with background density matrices obtained from the Lindblad equation using QTraj. Within this simplified treatment, the resulting medium-induced polarization is found to be very small while a naive rescaling for charmonium can qualitatively describe the polarization of charmonium.

title: Dynamics of self-gravitating halos with decaying dark matter
summary: We study the evolution of self-gravitating spherical dark matter halos composed of dark matter particles that decay to a slightly less massive particle and a massless particle. The small kick velocity imparted to the daughter particle upon decay heats the halo. If the kick velocity is small compared with the characteristic velocity, the halo remains bound but puffs out. We also consider, for the first time, decaying halos with anisotropic initial conditions and find non-negligible effects on the resulting density profile. To simulate the halo evolution, we utilize the recently developed \texttt{NSphere} code across a broad range of decay times and kick velocities. We train an emulator to provide a mapping between the decay parameters and the relaxed density profile. We discuss how the resulting halo-scale signatures complement existing cosmological constraints on decaying dark matter and can be tested by upcoming surveys.

title: Exact Splitting of Amplitudes and One-Loop Integrands: A Classical Origin of Zeros
summary: We introduce a recursion based on hidden zeros that reconstructs complete tree level scattering amplitudes and one-loop integrands at generic kinematics. The recursion takes a universal exact-splitting form: both tree amplitudes and one-loop surface integrands are expressed as sums of products of complete tree functions, with the chosen zero conditions manifest in every term. We establish this structure for cubic scalar theory, the nonlinear sigma model, and inverse string Kawai--Lewellen--Tye (KLT) functions. We derive the tree splitting formula from the equations of motion, showing that hidden zeros arise when the product of two currents solves the equations of motion, while corrections away from the zero reconstruct the full amplitude. We further show that inverse KLT is the unique extension of $\mathrm{Tr}(φ^3)$ with higher-point non-derivative interactions that preserves hidden zeros.

title: Quasi-equilibrium tidal folds of white dwarfs around rotating black holes in shift-symmetric Einstein--scalar--Gauss--Bonnet gravity
summary: We examine how the geometry of rotating black holes in linear, shift-symmetric Einstein--scalar--Gauss--Bonnet (EsGB) gravity changes the limiting tidal equilibria of white dwarfs (WDs). The relativistic tidal field is obtained from numerical EsGB backgrounds in a parallel-transported frame and coupled to a compressible affine model. Comparisons with Kerr black holes matched in Arnowitt--Deser--Misner (ADM) mass and angular momentum show a positive shift in the orbital frequency at the tidal fold. At fixed spin the relative correction follows an approximately quadratic dependence on the EsGB coupling, consistent with the leading response of the metric to the scalar field. Over the sampled backgrounds, the relative correction reaches order $10^{-3}$. Black hole rotation also changes the relation between the tidal fold and the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO): the sampled prograde folds remain outside the ISCO, while retrograde folds move inside it at higher spins. Orbital orientation therefore controls whether tidal equilibrium is lost before the orbital stability limit is reached. For the stellar and black hole masses considered here, the characteristic gravitational wave (GW) frequencies fall in the millihertz band relevant to planned space based interferometers. Future GW observations capable of resolving deviations from Kerr predictions could constrain the EsGB coupling.

title: Mock CSST NUV-NIR imaging of TNG50 galaxies with resolved stellar populations
comment: 14 pages, 13 figures, 5 tables, accepted for publication in A&A
summary: Aims. We aim to develop a framework for producing CSST-like mock images of resolved stellar populations from simulated galaxies, demonstrated here using two TNG50 galaxies as illustrative test cases. Methods. Starting from simulated galaxies from TNG50, we use the population synthesis code TRILEGAL to sample individual stars from star particles, retaining bright stars explicitly and treating the remaining unresolved light, including faint stellar light and nebular emission from star-forming regions, as a diffuse background component of the galaxy. Based on the dust distribution inferred from the gas mass and metallicity of gas cells, we use the radiative transfer (RT) code SKIRT to construct the dust model. From this model, we compute the line-of-sight extinction for individual stars, while image-level transmission maps for the diffuse light are derived through RT simulations. For young stars still embedded in their natal molecular clouds, we additionally include birth-cloud attenuation. The resulting dust-attenuated stellar catalogues and diffuse-light images are then processed with the CSST simulation pipeline, which applies PSF convolution, sky background, and instrumental noise.
