Results. Our framework produces mock CSST images for both a spiral galaxy and a dwarf irregular galaxy from TNG50 in the seven photometric bands. The mock images combine resolved stars, unresolved diffuse light, and dust attenuation within a unified framework, and include the main observational effects expected for the survey. The images are provided with known astrometric and photometric calibration information, and are intended as realistic image-level inputs for subsequent source detection, photometric recovery, and completeness analyses of resolved stellar populations. The framework is designed to be adaptable to other hydrodynamic simulations and observing configurations.

title: Light (anti)nuclei production via coalescence in electron-proton collisions: from HERA to EIC
comment: to appear on the proceedings of DIS 2026
summary: Light (anti)nuclei production provides a sensitive probe of the particle-emitting source and of the coalescence mechanism in high-energy collisions. In this work, a coalescence model implemented as an afterburner to PYTHIA 8 is validated against pp data from ALICE and ep data from ZEUS. The validated framework is then applied to ep collisions at EIC energies to predict deuteron and antideuteron production within the ePIC acceptance. The results indicate sizeable yields and a clear matter-antimatter asymmetry in the proton-going direction, making this measurement a promising observable for studying coalescence and proton structure at the EIC.

title: Euclid. Predicting scaling relations for emission-line galaxies using simulated data
comment: 12 pages, 9 figures, 5 pages appendix, submitted for publication to A&A
summary: The Euclid spectroscopic surveys will substantially increase the number of observed emission-line galaxies. We assess the ability of the Euclid Wide Survey (EWS) and Euclid Deep Survey (EDS), at the final DR3 depth, to recover the star-forming main sequence (MS), dust-mass relation (DMR), and mass-metallicity relation (MZR) from emission-line measurements. We use MAMBO (mocks with abundance matching in Bologna) spectroscopic simulations processed with the official Euclid pipelines. The MS is traced over $0\leq z\leq 4$ using Pa$β$, H$α$, and [OII] as SFR tracers. The shallow EWS flux limit biases the MS towards higher normalisation and a flatter slope by selecting the brightest, most strongly star-forming galaxies. The deeper EDS enables almost complete sampling with Pa$β$ and H$α$ at log$_{10}(M_*/M_\odot)\geq10.3$ over $0\leq z\leq 1.88$, with mild biases at both redshift limits. The [OII]-based MS is increasingly biased towards higher SFRs at the highest redshifts. The DMR is traced through the Balmer decrement over $1.45\leq z\leq 1.88$ and $0.9\leq z\leq 1.88$ in the EWS and EDS, respectively. The derived colour excess agree well with the input values, although detecting the faint H$β$ line restricts the sample to less obscured galaxies at fixed $M_*$, particularly in the EWS; the DMR is better sampled in the EDS. Finally, a golden sample detected in multiple optical rest-frame emission lines at $1.49\leq z\leq 1.88$ recovers gas-phase metallicities with typical accuracy of 0.1 dex at log$_{10}(M_*/M_\odot)\geq10$, while lower-mass galaxies show biases up to 0.15 dex. Relative to H-band limited sample, this sample preferentially traces the upper MS and lower MZR. Despite the simplified simulations lacking effects such as mutual spectral contamination and detector persistence, these forecasts provide a benchmark for future Euclid spectroscopic analyses.

title: Anomaly effective actions for 4d $\mathcal{N}=1$ superconformal field theories
summary: We present a comprehensive analysis of the Wess-Zumino anomaly effective action of four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ superconformal field theories in components. After reviewing the coset construction of the Wess-Zumino action in the presence of an unbroken subgroup, the gauging of the conformal algebra and the Wess-Zumino effective action for non-supersymmetric conformal field theories with a U(1) symmetry in two and four dimensions, we revisit the superconformal anomalies of $\mathcal{N}=1$ conformal supergravity. Solving the Wess-Zumino consistency conditions we determine both the bosonic and fermionic superconformal anomalies in a two-parameter family of schemes, to quadratic order in the gravitino. Turning on a chiral compensator multiplet and identifying a local super-Poincaré subalgebra of the conformal supergravity algebra without gauge-fixing the coset symmetries, we employ the coset construction and the superconformal anomalies in order to evaluate the Wess-Zumino action for generic $\mathcal{N}=1$ superconformal field theories coupled to conformal supergravity. By construction, this action reproduces the Weyl, R-symmetry, and S-supersymmetry coset anomalies, but its transformation under the unbroken Poincaré supersymmetry differs from the corresponding anomaly of the conformal supergravity functional. We show that there exists a local functional of the coset-invariant old-minimal fields that, when added to the Wess-Zumino action, results in a generalized Wess-Zumino action that reproduces all anomalies of the conformal supergravity functional. The same local functional enables us to determine the super-Weyl anomalies and the Wess-Zumino action of old-minimal supergravity, providing a component version of the known superspace Wess-Zumino action.

title: Born-Infeld black holes in bumblebee gravity
summary: We construct exact static and spherically symmetric charged solutions in bumblebee gravity minimally coupled to Born--Infeld electrodynamics, taking into account a spacelike vector norm and a vanishing cosmological constant. An independently varied Lagrange multiplier enforces the norm constraint and acquires a radial profile determined by the transverse electromagnetic pressure. The solutions include purely radial configurations and configurations with constant or varying temporal amplitudes. At $ξ=κ/2$, the varying temporal amplitude introduces an independent bumblebee field strength while preserving the metric of the constant temporal configuration. Moreover, the electric field remains bounded, and the temporal configurations admit smooth extensions across a simple future horizon under explicit regularity conditions. We derive the photon sphere and shadow radii for both metric and nonlinear electromagnetic propagation. The leading nonlinear corrections enlarge the shadow at fixed geometric charge, whereas the temporal amplitude enters through the charged lapse. Comparisons with observations of Sgr~A$^*$ and M87$^*$ provide conditional bounds on the charge and nonlinear scale. In addition, the adopted planetary perihelion allowances yield an illustrative sensitivity of $|ξ|(b^2+u_0^2)\lesssim2.6\times10^{-12}$ for a neutral solar exterior.

title: Spectroscopy-informed Deep Learning Searches for Photometric Little Red Dots in JWST Surveys
comment: 11 figures (9 in the main text and 2 additional in appendix), 5 tables, to appear in ApJS soon 35 new LRD candidates with NIRSpec/PRISM are identified
summary: Little Red Dots (LRDs) are a population of compact, red sources discovered at high redshift with JWST that exhibit distinctive V-shaped spectral energy distributions (SEDs). Existing LRD samples are typically identified using a variety of color-based selection criteria, which can lead to differences in the populations recovered by different studies. We develop a cross-modal machine-learning framework that combines matched NIRCam imaging and NIRSpec/PRISM spectroscopy to transfer spectroscopic information into imaging-based representations, enabling LRD identification from JWST/NIRCam imaging alone. Applied to spectroscopically observed high-redshift galaxies previously classified as non-LRDs, our model identifies 35 new LRD candidates. The majority satisfy at least one independent LRD color selection criterion, and among the 13 candidates with medium- or high-resolution NIRSpec grating spectra, 10 exhibit broad H$α$ emission - a hallmark of LRDs. We further apply the classifier to public NIRCam imaging from the Dawn JWST Archive and two independent JWST surveys, yielding 357 and 23 additional LRD candidates, respectively. The candidates recovered by our method span a broader range of observed SED properties than those in existing samples, suggesting that current color-selected samples may not fully capture the diversity of LRD-like systems present in JWST surveys. Our findings highlight the value of spectroscopy-informed photometric classification as a powerful strategy for systematically mining large-area JWST imaging datasets and provide a practical framework for future studies of this emerging population.

title: Earthquake Forecast via Neutrino Tomography at the DUNE Baseline
summary: We investigate the sensitivity of accelerator-based neutrino oscillations to localized electron-density enhancements associated with seismic fault zones along the Fermilab SURF baseline of the Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment (DUNE). Motivated by the reactor antineutrino proposal of Wang, Chen, and Li, we model the anomaly as a uniform-density slab embedded in the surrounding crust and calculate exact three flavour oscillation probabilities using layer by layer evolution. Our results show that localized density enhancements can produce measurable variations in muon-to-electron appearance probabilities for both neutrinos and antineutrinos, with potentially significant relative effects. The predicted variations exhibit weak dependence on the leptonic CP violating phase, suggesting that time-differential measurements may help reduce uncertainties associated with the unknown CP phase. However, the event statistics required for a statistically significant detection substantially exceed those expected during a short-duration precursor interval. Consequently, detecting sufficiently persistent density anomalies may be possible under favourable conditions, whereas short-term earthquake forecasting is not feasible with the nominal DUNE configuration. Our findings establish a theoretical framework for exploring localized Earth-density perturbations through long-baseline neutrino oscillations.

title: Euclid: Forecasting the number counts of bright line emitters in the Euclid Wide Survey and Euclid Deep fields
summary: The Euclid mission will revolutionize our understanding of the visible Universe by collecting images and spectra of millions of galaxies across cosmic time and environments. Here, we forecast the number counts of galaxies emitting [OII], H\b{eta}, [OIII], Hα and Pa\b{eta} lines in the Euclid Wide Survey (EWS) and Deep Survey (EDS). We compare predictions from different models, including semi-analytic models and empirical scaling relations. We then simulate spectra for galaxies in the MAMBO lightcone using FastSpec, designed to rapidly generate one-dimensional spectra as observed by Euclid. We process these simulated spectra with the official Euclid spectroscopic pipeline to recover redshifts and line fluxes and derive expected counts. Predictions for Hα+[NII] emitters are broadly consistent across mocks and with existing observations. In the EWS, relative RMS scatter among mock predictions for integrated counts is approximately 19% for Hα+[NII], 44% for [OII] and 41% for [OIII], reflecting greater model dependence for oxygen-line forecasts. After accounting for flux losses and redshift misidentification, corrected flux measurements recover most intrinsic line counts, especially in the EDS. From the MAMBO-based FastSpec simulations, we predict that Euclid will detect about 42 million Hα emitters in the EWS and 1.7 million in the EDS. The same simulations predict approximately 0.5 and 0.8 million [OII] and [OIII] emitters, respectively, in the EDS, and about 1.3 and 7.5 million in the EWS. These non-Hα forecasts remain subject to substantial model-dependent uncertainties, as shown by scatter among the different mocks. These samples will be instrumental in pushing large-scale structure and baryon acoustic oscillation studies beyond redshift z~2, extending Euclid cosmological and galaxy evolution studies beyond what is achievable with Hα alone.

title: Conformal field theory from automorphic forms on a quantum group
summary: We reformulate two-dimensional conformal field theory (2d CFT) in the language of noncommutative geometry. To this end, we introduce automorphic forms for the von Neumann algebraic quantum group $\mathrm{SL}^+_b(2,\mathbb{R})$. A quantum measure space is a von Neumann algebra equipped with a weight. We study such spaces carrying a weight-preserving action of $\mathrm{SL}^+_b(2,\mathbb{R})$. We argue that every unitary bosonic 2d CFT with central charge $c=1+6(b+b^{-1})^2>1$ is equivalent to a quantum measure space with an action of $\mathrm{SL}^+_b(2,\mathbb{R})\times\mathrm{SL}^+_b(2,\mathbb{R})$. In this dictionary, Virasoro primary operators are quantum automorphic forms and their scaling dimensions correspond to the spectrum of a quantum Laplace operator. The Virasoro crossing equations express associativity of multiplication on the quantum measure space. For compact theories, the algebra is a type III$_1$ factor. Liouville CFT is realized as $\mathrm{SL}^+_b(2,\mathbb{R})$ acting on itself by left and right translations. Virasoro boundary conditions correspond to quantum measure spaces with an action of a single copy of $\mathrm{SL}^+_b(2,\mathbb{R})$. When the boundary spectrum is discrete, these are noncommutative counterparts of compact hyperbolic surfaces. The formulation accommodates models both with and without extended chiral algebras. It bridges the Virasoro conformal bootstrap with categorical and von Neumann algebraic approaches to 2d CFT.

title: Inflationary attractors in metric-affine gravity
summary: We study single-field slow-roll inflation in metric-affine gravity (MAG). We consider the most general action up to operators linear in curvature and quadratic in the distortion, without propagating torsion and non-metricity. We first impose projective invariance and promote every coefficient to a function of the scalar field. After integrating out the non-dynamical distortion, the net contribution is a correction $k(φ)$ to the scalar kinetic term. We then consider the class of $ξ$-attractors for which the non-minimal couplings and the scalar potential are fixed by a single function $f(φ)$. It is well-known that in the metric formulation the strong-coupling regime is universally the Starobinsky attractor. In the Palatini framework, instead, this attractor is lost and the predictions become model-dependent. Here, we show that the MAG framework restores universality: in the strong coupling limit with finite ratios of the distortion couplings to $ξ$ we have an $α$-attractor, $n_s=1-2/N_*$ and $r=12α/N_*^2$, with $α=1+ζ/(6ξ)$. The ratio $ζ/ξ$ encodes the distortion contribution. Starobinsky and Palatini inflation are recovered as specific limits. Through a numerical parameter scan we show that almost all the healthy points lie on one of the two attractors : either Nieh-Yan-like inflation (studied in a previous work and extended here) or the new MAG $α$-attractor found here. Finally, we explicitly drop projective invariance and analyse the general MAG theory. The same large-field asymptotic structure survives. We conclude that no extra inflationary phenomenology is reached by the non-projectively invariant operators: the $α$-attractor is a general prediction of MAG.

title: Aperture-dependent [O III] profile variability: Clues to the nature of double-peaked narrow emission lines
summary: We propose a simple and practical aperture-dependent method for investigating the physical origin of double-peaked narrow emission lines (DPNELs). Spectroscopic observations obtained from different apertures probe different spatial regions and therefore different gas kinematics within the narrow line region (NLR). Consequently, changes in the profiles of DPNELs observed with different apertures can provide important constraints on their physical origins. We applied this method to SDSS J0941 by comparing spectra obtained from the SDSS, DESI, and LAMOST surveys. Significant differences are found in the double-peaked profiles of the different spectra, demonstrating that aperture effects can strongly influence the integrated DPNEL profiles. The AGN model, where the two nuclei lie in a plane perpendicular to the line of sight, can qualitatively explain the asymmetric sampling of the two NLRs, but it cannot explain the different peak separations of different spectra. The observed asymmetric evolution of the two components disfavors a simple AGN-driven outflow and a rotating disk-like NLR scenario. Of the models considered, only a more complex non-axisymmetric rotating NLR provides a self-consistent explanation for the observed aperture-dependent variations. In this scenario, the blueshifted emitting region is more compact and remains largely enclosed by the smaller aperture, resulting in an increased line width with little change in flux. In contrast, the redshifted emitting region is more spatially extended and is therefore more strongly affected by the reduced aperture, leading to pronounced decreases in both flux and line width. Our results illustrate the diagnostic potential of combining multi-aperture spectroscopic surveys to study DPNEL origins, while highlighting the difficulty of distinguishing between physical scenarios.

title: Born spreading with consistent shower starting scales in MC@NLO and FxFx merging
summary: Negative weights are a major cost in NLO event generation matched to parton showers at the LHC, as they increase the number of events needed for a given statistical precision. Born spreading reduces the fraction of negative-weight $\mathbb S$ events in MC@NLO by redistributing the Born contribution over the radiation variables. It introduces no bias only if everything that is passed to the parton shower together with $\mathbb S$ events depends on Born-level quantities alone. We show that the same condition is needed for the MC counterterms to reproduce the first shower emission, independently of how the radiation phase space is integrated. In MadGraph5_aMC@NLO, the $\mathbb S$-event starting scales did not fully satisfy this condition, which so far prevented the public release of Born spreading. We present a new and consistent construction of the starting scales for ordinary MC@NLO, FxFx merging and MC@NLO-$Δ$, with which Born spreading is now publicly available, including for merged samples. We also study modified formulations of the MC counterterms, and FxFx-merged $W$+jets production with up to two jets at NLO, for which Born spreading reduces the fraction of negative weights after merging without affecting the predictions, and the event samples are generated six times faster than with the former implementation.

title: DESI DR2 Results III: The Mass of the Milky Way
comment: This paper is a DESI Collaboration Key Project publication. 25+12 pages, 14+2 figures, 5+1 tables. Submitted to ApJ
summary: We present measurements of the mass of the Milky Way using distant halo stars selected from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) Data Release 2 (DR2). We apply four dynamical modeling methods to 10,036 RR Lyrae (RRL) and blue horizontal branch (BHB) stars with 6D phase space coordinates that span from $\sim$10 to 95 kpc from the Galactic center, the largest samples of their kind. All methods are applied to mock surveys based on cosmological simulations that include generating individual tracer stars, convolving their phase-space coordinates with DESI and Gaia DR3-like uncertainties, and tailored models of the survey selection functions. By comparing the performance on these mocks, we quantify how systematic biases from both methodology assumptions and galaxy disequilibrium impact each estimate. The mock-based systematics, which differ by method and tracer, are used to correct the individual estimates and to derive joint estimates using a rigorous formalism that accounts for per-method biases and residual correlations between methods. We obtain a joint estimate of the mass within 80 kpc to be $M(r < 80 \mathrm{\,kpc}) = 6.36^{+0.53}_{-0.48} \times 10^{11}$ M$_\odot$ and a virial mass estimate of $M_\mathrm{200c} = 1.19^{+0.14}_{-0.12} \times 10^{12}$ M$_\odot$, with similar results when combining only RRL-based or BHB-based measurements. These results provide a roadmap for future DESI efforts, as well as those in other spectroscopic surveys, to reliably constrain the mass of our Galaxy.

title: Axial black hole perturbations in purely-metric Horndeski theories
summary: We study axial (odd-parity) perturbations about static and spherically-symmetric curvaturised black hole solutions of purely-metric Horndeski theories. We first review the construction of purely-metric theories of gravity with second-order equations of motion and an additional propagating scalar degree of freedom which is purely gravitational. We then revisit the formation, in a subclass of these theories, of a new branch of hairy black hole solutions under tachyonic instabilities of the scalar field near the Schwarzschild solution. Because a non-zero Ricci curvature grows and by analogy with black hole scalarisation, the latter black hole formation mechanism is dubbed \emph{curvaturisation}. We then apply the first-order approach to the dynamics of axial perturbations and find that it is equivalent to that of axial perturbations in general relativity evolving in a distinct effective metric. We explicitly provide that effective metric in terms of the background and the Lagrangian functions, and show that it shares the same causality structure as the background metric of curvaturised black holes. By turning to the Schrödinger-like formulation of the perturbations, we analyse the scattering potential and conclude that the axial perturbations of curvaturised black holes are linearly stable. Finally, we confirm these findings by explicitly computing the fundamental quasi-normal mode as well as the first five overtones for the quadrupole $\ell = 2$.

title: Evolutionary Map of the Universe (EMU): Selection of active galactic nuclei and star-formation emission with machine-learning techniques
comment: Accepted for publication in A&A, 19 pages, 20 figures, and two tables
summary: Sources detected by recent large-area radio surveys require robust classification and characterisation. The Evolutionary Map of the Universe (EMU) is a prime example of machine-learning (ML) techniques efficiently enriching existing catalogues with classifications and derived physical properties that would be impractical to obtain from spectroscopy or colour selection alone. We aim to build a labelled sample of sources in the EMU pilot survey (EMU-PS, at 944 MHz, with rms ~ 30 uJy/beam over 270 deg2 in the southern sky) classified as being dominated by active galactic nuclei (AGNs) or non-AGN processes including star-formation. We will then use this sample to examine radio properties and redshift-dependent trends. We applied a pre-trained multi-stage ML pipeline to optical-to-infrared photometry of EMU-PS sources to derive classifications and photometric redshifts, which we used to compute additional radio properties, including luminosities. We increase the known number of AGNs and non-AGNs in the EMU-PS by more than a factor of 15 (recall 96 %) up to z ~ 5, and by nearly a factor of 100 (recall 94 %) for z > 1, respectively. In extrapolating these numbers for the full EMU survey, we expect to recover more than 3.4 million AGN candidates. A non-negligible low-redshift subsample of selected non-AGNs shows radio luminosities in excess of those expected from star formation alone, revealing detachment between photometric and radio classification. Radio-derived properties show expected trends for luminosities and a lack of evolution for in-band (800-1088 MHz) spectral indices. The ML-based pipeline provides a scalable way to produce large catalogues for the ongoing EMU survey and future Square Kilometre Array observations and reveals that multi-wavelength analysis can uncover radio populations and trends often missed by colour cuts or spectroscopy alone.

title: Ground-State Heavy-Baryon Mass Spectrum in the Relativistic Independent Quark Model
summary: We extend our work to compute the ground-state baryon mass spectrum containing charm and bottom quarks in the relativistic independent quark (RIQ) model with an average flavor--independent confining potential in equally mixed scalar--vector harmonic form. Each quark moves as a Dirac particle inside the potential. The resulting core mass is then corrected perturbatively, accounting for the pion self-energy, pion exchange, and pairwise color--electric and color--magnetic one-gluon exchange. Six input parameters common to every baryon: the potential parameters (confinement strength, the potential offset) and the $u(=d)$, $s$, $c$, and $b$ constituent quark masses are optimized using a few experimentally measured baryon states. The model then uses these optimized parameters to predict the mass spectra of doubly heavy, mixed-$bc$, and triply heavy baryons. We compare our predictions with lattice QCD, relativistic quark model results, and available experimental measurements. Our results are consistent with these model predictions and experimental results.

title: The Cosmology of Hawking Axions
summary: Since primordial black holes (PBH) are always non-relativistic, their cosmological energy fraction grows relative to that of radiation. Thus, for even a tiny initial PBH abundance, the universe generically enters an epoch of early matter domination, which ends when the PBH evaporate to restore the hot big bang. We consider the possibility that a PBH dominated era yields a population of boosted axion-like particles (ALPs) produced from Hawking evaporation. title: Parton wave functions, density matrices and entropy in DGLAP evolution
summary: Parton multiplicity entropy, proposed by Kharzeev and Levin as entanglement between the region probed in deep inelastic scattering and the proton's remainder, was compared with hadron multiplicity data. It is computed from parton densities, which do not fix the partons' quantum state. We show that a one-parton density matrix from Lipatov's wave functions determines two entropies for resolved modes with finite mean number and entropy. Its trace is the mean parton number, and normalization gives a sampled parton's entropy. A compatible thermal state, if it exists, maximizes entropy at fixed one-parton matrix. This maximum equals the actual entropy only for that thermal state and measures entanglement only for a specified subsystem of a pure state. The geometric multiplicity entropy follows if all emitted partons share one mode. An entropy computed from densities becomes such a maximum, an upper bound on the actual entropy, only for specified resolved modes. We also show that the state averaged over unrecorded emissions, assumed incoherent across scales, obeys probability-preserving Lindblad evolution on finitely many regulated modes with the resolution scale if emission and no-emission terms match. The occupations reproduce leading-order DGLAP, with virtual terms, at leading logarithmic accuracy as the cutoffs on momentum fractions are removed. The reduction holds for strongly ordered transverse momenta in light-cone gauge and dilute occupations, including those of newly resolved modes. Approximating momentum and helicity modes by independent thermal populations closes the occupation equation and gives this bound's evolution, with Bose and Pauli factors from the operator algebra. We propose testing this approximation at HERA or the LHC. The test compares the mode number inferred from normalized hadron factorial moments in a rapidity window with the window's transverse mode count.

title: Gravitational-Wave Constraints on $R^2$ Gravity
summary: Gravitational waves from compact binary coalescences provide a unique opportunity to test general relativity in the strong-field regime. Quadratic $f(R)=R+aR^2$ gravity is among the simplest higher-curvature extensions of general relativity and introduces a massive scalar degree of freedom whose finite interaction range can modify compact-binary dynamics and gravitational-wave emission. We map this theory onto the effective-field-theory waveform for generic massive scalar-tensor gravity, obtaining a theory-specific inspiral phase correction governed by the single coupling parameter $a$. Using Bayesian analyses of the binary-neutron-star events GW170817 and GW190425, we obtain a combined constraint on the quadratic-curvature coupling of $a\lesssim6.2\times10^6\,\mathrm{m}^2$ at $90\%$ credibility, corresponding to a lower bound on the scalar mass of $m_s\gtrsim3.2\times10^{-11}\,\mathrm{eV}$. This constitutes the strongest astrophysical constraint on the quadratic-curvature coupling, improving the previous best bound by approximately five orders of magnitude and demonstrating the sensitivity of binary-neutron-star inspirals to finite-range scalar interactions in the strong-field regime.

title: A brief overview of the baryon cycle in galaxies
summary: Galaxy formation and evolution is governed by the continuous exchange of gas between the cosmic web, the circumgalactic medium (CGM), and the interstellar medium (ISM) of galaxies. This brief review summarises our current understanding of this baryon cycle, from the accretion of gas onto galaxies to its conversion into stars, and the feedback processes that regulate the growth of galaxies. Several open questions will be highlighted, that will encourage progresses in cosmological simulations, multiwavelength observations, and theory to resolve.

title: Cross-Moment Consistency and the Fifth Adler Coefficient in Hadronic Tau Decays
summary: The unknown coefficient $c_{5,1}$ controls the first omitted fifth-order term in fixed-order analyses of inclusive hadronic $τ$ decays. We determine what the four known Adler coefficients can actually test. For any normalized polynomial weight, the fixed-order Adler-to-moment map is triangular with unit diagonal. Hence one common Adler-coefficient error reaches every moment with the same absolute size, and a multi-weight relative test reduces to one absolute tolerance. For three representative weights, a ten-percent test resolves $c_{5,1}$ only to about $\pm24$; the closest contour-improved test is weaker by more than an order of magnitude. Moreover, any continuation that preserves the observed sign of the direct Padé/Shanks defects gives $c_{5,1}\geq378.03$, so values near $280$ require additional structure. A calibration-and-falsification protocol applied to a simplified Beneke--Jamin-type pure-power ansatz gives the conditional estimate $c_{5,1}=248\pm30\,(\mathrm{struct})\pm74\,(\mathrm{method})=248\pm80$. At the physical order its central value coincides algebraically with the exact four-parameter fit; the protocol adds a falsifiable admissibility test and a method uncertainty, not new coefficient information. We also clarify that the often-quoted Beneke--Jamin value $283$ is a linear extrapolation of total-width FOPT te

title: Spacetime Evolution Induced by a Massive Cosmic String in Numerical Relativity
summary: Cosmic strings are one-dimensional topological defects formed during phase transitions in the early universe. ''Massive'' cosmic strings possess a sufficiently large tension to close their transverse space, forming a conical singularity outside the string, as a static gravitational effect. In a dynamical context, such strings are expected to drive topological inflation. In this work, we investigate the spacetime evolution induced by the formation of a massive cosmic string in a radiation-dominated cosmological background, imposing cylindrical symmetry. Using full numerical relativity simulations, we observe that the string core undergoes topological inflation and that its boundary moves inwards superluminally, which causally disconnects the core from the outer universe. Between the core and the asymptotic regions, a nearly matter-dominated decelerating region originates sourced by the oscillating string fields. This region is bounded by a local maximum (''belly'') and local minimum (''throat'') of the circumferential radius, while the throat recedes outwards at about 10% the speed of light. Furthermore, a gravitational wavefront is emitted from the string, characterizing the light cone of the string formation. Even behind the wavefront, the exterior region no longer exhibits a ''conical'' structure. Based on the simulation results, we construct a Penrose diagram, reflecting the causal structure of the entire spacetime.

title: The Start Time of Ringdown
summary: We determine the convergence of quasi-normal modes sums for a point-particle plunging into a Schwarzschild black hole. While a dynamical amplitude model reproduces the waveform after the particle crosses the bounce radius, a constant amplitude sum converges only after the start time $t_S$, which corresponds to the advanced time at which the particle hits the central singularity. For a plunge from the ISCO, $t_S \simeq 9.4 M$ after the peak of the $22$ mode. After $t_S$, dynamical and constant amplitudes models are equivalent; our analysis also implies that any "direct wave" must reduce to the late-time tail after $t_S$.

title: Quiescent galaxies at cosmic noon: from individual element abundances to star formation histories
comment: 8 pages, 2 figures, published on New Astronomy
summary: Understanding the formation and early evolution of massive quiescent galaxies is crucial for a complete picture of galaxy formation in a cosmological context. Such a comprehensive picture can be obtained through measurements of individual elemental abundances, which encode the timescales and physical conditions of their star-formation and assembly histories. While extensive work at low and intermediate redshift has revealed strong correlations between stellar mass, metallicity, and abundance ratios, studies at z ~ 2-3 remain extremely limited. Their faintness and compactness make medium-resolution near-infrared spectroscopy for detailed chemical analysis extremely challenging. We present a science case to measure full elemental abundance patterns in a representative sample of massive quiescent galaxies at cosmic noon, exploiting rest-frame optical absorption features. We show that deriving robust stellar population constraints for these systems requires spectra with S/N ~ 20 per resolution element, together with a spatial resolution comparable to their ~ 0.1 arcsec sizes. We show that such requirements can only be met with a 40m class telescope equipped with a powerful adaptive optics system. In this context, SHARP-NEXUS, in combination with MORFEO-MCAO capabilities, emerges as the only viable ELT instrument capable of enabling this science, providing both the sensitivity and angular resolution needed. Although massive quiescent galaxies are rare at these redshifts, their study can efficiently exploit the instrument's multiplexing by targeting galaxy overdensities and coordinating with surveys of star-forming galaxies. Such synergistic strategies, proven feasible in high-redshift clusters and by multiplex-sharing facilities like 4MOST, would allow SHARP-NEXUS to open a new window on the chemical enrichment of the earliest massive galaxies.

title: Inflationary attractors in metric-affine gravity
summary: We study single-field slow-roll inflation in metric-affine gravity (MAG). We consider the most general action up to operators linear in curvature and quadratic in the distortion, without propagating torsion and non-metricity. We first impose projective invariance and promote every coefficient to a function of the scalar field. After integrating out the non-dynamical distortion, the net contribution is a correction $k(φ)$ to the scalar kinetic term. We then consider the class of $ξ$-attractors for which the non-minimal couplings and the scalar potential are fixed by a single function $f(φ)$. It is well-known that in the metric formulation the strong-coupling regime is universally the Starobinsky attractor. In the Palatini framework, instead, this attractor is lost and the predictions become model-dependent. Here, we show that the MAG framework restores universality: in the strong coupling limit with finite ratios of the distortion couplings to $ξ$ we have an $α$-attractor, $n_s=1-2/N_*$ and $r=12α/N_*^2$, with $α=1+ζ/(6ξ)$. The ratio $ζ/ξ$ encodes the distortion contribution. Starobinsky and Palatini inflation are recovered as specific limits. Through a numerical parameter scan we show that almost all the healthy points lie on one of the two attractors : either Nieh-Yan-like inflation (studied in a previous work and extended here) or the new MAG $α$-attractor found here. Finally, we explicitly drop projective invariance and analyse the general MAG theory. The same large-field asymptotic structure survives. We conclude that no extra inflationary phenomenology is reached by the non-projectively invariant operators: the $α$-attractor is a general prediction of MAG.

title: The quasi-topological space of quasi-topological gravities
summary: We investigate general properties of quasi-topological theories of gravity involving infinite towers of polynomial densities and of their regular vacuum black hole solutions. We show that every positive-mass regular vacuum solution necessarily possesses a de Sitter core, while Minkowski and anti-de Sitter cores are excluded. Regarding the horizon structure, we prove that asymptotically flat and anti-de Sitter regular black holes always admit extremal configurations. We find that there is no upper bound on the number of horizons and that horizons of arbitrarily high degeneracy can arise. These results extend to more general theories of gravity with second-order equations on spherically symmetric backgrounds. Finally, we characterize the space of quasi-topological theories admitting regular black holes, showing that it is contractible (in particular, path-connected and simply connected) and that regularity is stable under suitably small deformations of the higher-order couplings. In the sense of Spanier, this space is naturally a contractible \emph{quasi-topological} space. Additionally, we prove that any theory defined by a set of couplings up to any arbitrarily high, but finite, curvature order can be completed into a theory yielding regular black hole solutions, while preserving the same set of lower-order couplings. title: An obstruction to cosmic acceleration from shift-symmetric dark sector interactions
summary: Using the effective field theory of cosmological media, we show that derivative interactions in the dark sector between a perfect fluid and a superfluid cannot support slow-roll expansion while remaining free from instabilities. Furthermore, decomposing the dark sector medium into effective dark matter and dark energy components, we find that the stability conditions exclude a phantom-to-non-phantom crossing. Our approach gives a clear route for constructing theoretically viable dark sector models, and highlights the fundamental constraints that stability requirements impose on their cosmological dynamics.

title: Understanding galaxies and the origin of the golden mass through the study of scaling relations across cosmic history
comment: 13 pages, 2 figures. Accepted for publication in the New Astronomy Special Issue: SHARP Science Book
summary: The total mass distribution in galaxies strongly influences star formation (SF), both directly via gas availability and feedback, and indirectly via the dark matter (DM) potential well. This scale also appears in other scaling relations: correlations between stellar population gradients, DM fraction, and total mass density slope versus stellar mass all show pronounced minima at the golden mass. How, why, and when does this golden mass emerge during galaxy evolution? Early cosmic epochs ($z > 1.5$) remain largely unexplored, yet they probe the formative stages of galaxy mass assembly. They provide the full redshift baseline needed to constrain the buildup of stellar mass and the efficiency of gas-to-star conversion. By combining high resolution, multiplexing, and a wide field of view, SHARP on the ELT will address these questions, delivering sharper and deeper data than JWST. In this SHARP White Paper contribution, we present a scientific case exploiting these unique characteristics. SHARP will enable precise measurements of stellar population gradients, DM fractions, and total mass density slopes. Using the mIFU mode, SHARP will obtain spatially-resolved stellar population and dynamical maps for galaxies at $z > 1.5$. Reconstructing these observables for early- and late-type systems will allow us to trace the emergence of the golden mass across cosmic time, and to decode the impact of galaxy processes (mergers, SN, and AGN feedback) by comparing observations with cosmological simulations. title: Dynamics of self-gravitating halos with decaying dark matter
summary: We study the evolution of self-gravitating spherical dark matter halos composed of dark matter particles that decay to a slightly less massive particle and a massless particle. We also consider, for the first time, decaying halos with anisotropic initial conditions and find non-negligible effects on the resulting density profile. To simulate the halo evolution, we utilize the recently developed \texttt{NSphere} code across a broad range of decay times and kick velocities. We train an emulator to provide a mapping between the decay parameters and the relaxed density profile. We discuss how the resulting halo-scale signatures complement existing cosmological constraints on decaying dark matter and can be tested by upcoming surveys.

title: Gravitational waves flooding the Universe after wall domination
summary: We discuss a possible early Universe scenario, where radiation era is interrupted by the epoch of domination of domain walls eventually annihilating into particles. During this period the Universe undergoes accelerated expansion, while the comoving correlation length of the domain wall network remains constant. The network serves as a source of tensor modes, which get frozen upon exiting the horizon similarly to the case of inflationary fluctuations. The modes re-enter the horizon during the subsequent stage of radiation domination and since then contribute to the gravitational wave background. The spectral shape of gravitational waves predicted in this scenario is markedly different compared to the case of domain walls remaining sub-dominant all the way till annihilation. These gravitational waves are strong enough to be observed with present-day and future facilities in a broad range of frequencies. In particular, their energy density is sufficient to produce a significant impact on the effective number of neutrino species, unless the duration of wall domination is suitably constrained.

title: Complex phase diagram and thermodynamic supercriticality of five-dimensional four-charge AdS black holes in $STU-W^2U$ gauged supergravity
summary: In this paper, we investigate the complex phase structure and thermodynamic supercriticality of static four-charge anti-de Sitter (AdS) black holes in five-dimensional $STU-W^2U$ gauged supergravity, with all four physical electric charges held fixed. A Van der Waals-like first-order small/large black hole phase transition is found to terminate at a critical point. By analytically continuing the fixed-charge thermodynamic relations, we trace the two real spinodal singularities through criticality into a complex-conjugate pair in the supercritical region. The corresponding spinodal temperatures exhibit the characteristic $3/2$ near-critical scaling, connecting the subcritical temperature splitting with the imaginary parts of the supercritical complex temperatures. We construct the associated complex phase diagram and identify a Widom-type crossover line from the real-temperature projection of the complex spinodals. This line progressively deviates from the locus of real heat-capacity maxima as the pressure increases. At higher pressures, the real heat-capacity extrema eventually merge and disappear, while the complex spinodal singularities persist. Together, these results reveal a continuous connection between critical phase transitions and supercritical thermodynamics through complex singularity structures, providing further insight into the thermodynamic phase behavior of multicharge supergravity black holes.

title: Supermassive black holes and nuclear star clusters in galaxies: constraining formation and co-evolution with SHARP and MICADO
comment: 8 pages, 1 figure. Contribution to the SHARP Science Book
summary: Nuclear star clusters and supermassive black holes are the dominant compact components in galaxy nuclei. They can coexist within the same system, and their relative prominence traces the history of gas inflow, star formation, and dynamical evolution on parsec scales. Key questions remain open concerning the physical channels that assemble nuclear star clusters, the mass regimes in which supermassive black holes become dynamically dominant, and the conditions under which compact stellar nuclei are suppressed, destroyed, or replaced by cusp-like structures. We describe how near-infrared integral-field spectroscopy with SHARP on the Extremely Large Telescope, combined with high-resolution imaging from MICADO, enables quantitative tests of nuclear formation and evolution scenarios within a unified framework. The joint analysis of stellar dynamics, stellar populations, and nuclear structure allows black-hole masses, internal kinematics of nuclear star clusters, and signatures of gas inflow to be measured consistently within the same systems, and defines the mass and distance ranges where robust constraints can be obtained. Recent discoveries of compact active nuclei at high redshift indicate that efficient black-hole growth can occur in systems with weak or compact stellar components. Although nearby galaxies are not evolutionary analogues of early systems, the diversity of nuclear configurations accessible with SHARP and MICADO provides a local laboratory for isolating the physical mechanisms that regulate the coupled evolution of central black holes and nuclear stellar structures.

title: Satisfying Freed--Witten quantization on smooth divisors in Calabi--Yau orientifolds
comment: 8+4 pages of main text and appendices
summary: Freed--Witten quantization conditions on several divisors wrapped by D-branes must be satisfied with one bulk $B$-field. On a smooth Calabi--Yau threefold $X$ with a holomorphic O3/O7 involution $σ$, we show that the common background $B_{2,+}^{\star}=\tfrac12[R]$, where $R$ is the total O7 divisor, permits Freed--Witten period quantization on the full two-cycle lattice of \emph{every smooth connected divisor}, modulo torsion. The worldvolume fluxes are chosen individually and obey the orientifold relation between each divisor and its image. The central step concerns setwise invariant divisors $D$: we prove that the bulk Freed--Witten class $η_D^\star=\tfrac12([R]+[D])|_D$ has integer periods on every $σ$-even integral two-cycle class, including inherited and autochthonous classes. Its periods on purely $σ$-odd classes vanish, so any remaining non-integer periods occur only on classes that are neither $σ$-even nor $σ$-odd. We show how to choose $σ$-odd worldvolume fluxes on these invariant divisors that make all periods integral. For exchanged divisor pairs, quantizing the flux on one member automatically quantizes its orientifold image. On invariant divisors with $h^{2,0}_-(D)=0$, the constructed flux is of type $(1,1)$ and admits a primitive representative; this includes every smooth rigid invariant divisor. We also study zero worldvolume flux on invariant divisors. For $h^{1,1}_-(X)\leq1$, we construct common bulk backgrounds satisfying every inherited intersection period on all such divisors. A binary compatibility test determines whether a common shift exists for larger $h^{1,1}_-(X)$. Non-inherited period tests then determine whether the resulting backgrounds allow zero flux on the full worldvolume lattices.

title: Net Cooling Tables for Cosmological Simulations under Multiple UV/X-ray Background Models
summary: We present three sets of net cooling tables for cosmological hydrodynamical simulations, computed with CLOUDY 23.01 for optically thin gas in photoionization equilibrium with three different UV/X-ray background models. For gas of Solar composition, the choice of UV/X-ray background has little impact on the net cooling rates at low redshift, but the results increasingly diverge towards high redshift, particularly in diffuse gas near thermal equilibrium. Compared with widely used previous tables, cooling times in this regime differ by up to an order of magnitude at $z \gtrsim 4.6$, and the calculations disagree on whether the gas undergoes net cooling or heating over nearly 10% of the diffuse density-temperature plane at $z \approx 8$, corresponding to the intergalactic medium. These trends persist for gas composed exclusively of hydrogen and helium. The tables provide a consistent framework for assessing the impact of the radiation background on gas cooling in cosmological simulations.

title: Goldstone theory of gluon saturation in high energy QCD: From color glass to color superfluid condensate
summary: In the high energy Regge asymptotics of QCD, the rapid overpopulation of gluons leads to gluon saturation, characterized by nonperturbative semi-classical lumpy configurations of size $1/Q_S$, where $Q_S\gg Λ_{\rm QCD}$ is a dynamical semi-hard saturation scale. We discuss here a generalization of the Color Glass Condensate (CGC) framework describing this phenomenon that is obtained by carefully treating the breaking of global symmetries by the condensate. In particular, we show that the breaking of a global subgroup of color results in a Goldstone effective field theory (EFT) whose dynamics is characterized by a Goldstone decay constant $f_G = \sqrt{N} Q_S$, where $N=O(1/α_S)$ is the phase space occupancy of the condensate, which is large for $α_S(Q_S)\ll 1$. Further, the coupling of these colored Goldstones to collinear gluon modes leads to a depletion of the condensate, thereby modifying the static shockwave scattering framework of the CGC on timescales controlled by $f_G$. The CGC EFT on these longer time scales is a novel color superfluid. Low frequency modes with $ω\leq α_S Q_S$ in an external probe of the CGC are sensitive to superfluid dynamics, with interesting physical consequences for deeply inelastic scattering and ultrarelativistic nuclear collisions.

title: Bumblebee radiation from neutral matter around a black hole
comment: 12 pages in double column and 5 figures
summary: We investigate bumblebee radiation generated by neutral matter orbiting a black hole with a radial spacelike vector vacuum. Starting from a point particle coupled minimally to the metric, we derive the curvature induced vector current and the potential response required by its conservation. For a localized circular source with no independent radial boundary current, this response gives $δV'=ξρ/4$. The axial vector source instead follows the radial transport of angular momentum and vanishes for circular motion. A slightly eccentric orbit excites an axial dipole at the orbital frequency $Ω$ and a quadrupole contribution at $2Ω$, with outgoing amplitudes proportional to $ev^3$ and $ev^4$, respectively, where $v=\sqrt{M/a}$. We construct their retarded response and obtain the leading coefficients through weak field matching. Reconstruction of the observer's tidal tensor gives the dipole strain $h_{\hat r\hatφ}^{V,10}=ξ^2b^2μev^3\sinθ\cos[Ω(t-R)]/(8πR)$. The corresponding partial luminosity is $P_{B,10}^{\infty}=ξ^2b^2μ^2e^2v^{12}/(48πM^2)$ at the leading order. Remarkably, the ordinary neutral matter produces an additional radial transverse tidal signal even when the homogeneous gravitational master operator remains in Schwarzschild form.

summary: The role of active galactic nuclei (AGNs) in the suppression of star formation and structural evolution of galaxies during their transition from star-forming to quiescent systems remains unclear. We analyze 3,955 AGNs selected through five multiwavelength diagnostics at $0<z<5$. Using high-resolution JWST imaging from the COSMOS-Web survey and archival multi-wavelength photometry, we investigate the rest-frame optical size-mass distribution of AGN host galaxies and compare it with those of star-forming galaxies (SFGs) and quiescent galaxies (QGs). We find that the positions of AGN hosts in the size-mass plane depend on both redshift and stellar mass. At $z\gtrsim2$, massive AGN hosts ($M_\star/M_\odot>10^{10.5}$) generally exhibit sizes comparable to those of SFGs despite suppressed star formation. Toward lower redshifts, they increasingly approach the QG size-mass relation, accompanied by declining specific star formation rates (sSFRs) and increasing Sérsic indices. In contrast, lower-mass AGN hosts remain close to the SFG relation across the redshift range. Overall, AGN hosts exhibit relatively mild size evolution, following $R_e\propto(1+z)^{-0.6}$ over $0<z<4$, shallower than that of typical SFGs and QGs. We further examine the relationship between star formation activity and structural compactness in the $Δ\log\mathrm{SFR}_{\mathrm{MS}}$-$ΔΣ_e$ plane. At $z<2.2$, AGN hosts predominantly occupy the compact star-forming and quiescent regions, broadly consistent with the compaction-quenching scenario. At $z>2.2$, however, some AGN hosts exhibit suppressed star formation while retaining relatively extended structures. These findings suggest that some AGN hosts may follow alternative evolutionary pathways in which star formation suppression precedes substantial structural compaction.
